CITY OF LOS ANGELES.

 

 

 

ORDINANCE No. 114.

An Orpinance to prevent fast riding and driving upon the public bridge in.the
City of Los Angeles, upon old Aliso road, and to protect all bridges in said
city from being injured or defaced.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows :

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person to ride, lead or drive any
‘wagon, carriage, buggy or other vehicle, or any kind of stock or cattle, upon,
over or across the public covered bridge extending across the Los Angeles River
upon old Aliso Road, in said city, at any rate of speed faster than a walk.

Se. 2. It shall be unlawful for any person to injure or deface any bridge
in said city by cutting the same, or by posting thereon any handbill, circular,
advertisement or other notice of any kind, or in any other manner whatever.

Src. 8. Any person violating any of the provisions of this ordinance, shall,
upon conviction thereof, be punished by a fine of not less than five dollars nor

more than one hundred dollars, or by imprisonment not less than five nor more
than one hundred days, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Sxc. 4. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

' Se. 6. That ordinance adopted by the Council of the City of Los Angeles,
on July 10, 1880, and appsowts by the Mayor of said city, on July 14, 1880, is
hereby repealed.

===== PDF PAGE 012 [contrast-enhanced] =====
6 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 6. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HERALD, a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter wt
shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of December 24, A. D. 1883.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

ORDINANCE No. 115.

AN OrDINANCE granting a franchise for a street railroad in the City of Los
Angeles to the Central Railway Company.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the reasonable right of way be, and the same is hereby
granted to the Central Railway Company, over and along the following named
public streets of said city, for the period of twenty years from and after the date
of the passage of this ordinance, for the purpose of laying down, operating and
maintaining one line of street railroad track, and all necessary turnouts and
switches, and with two parallel iron rails, the rails to be what are known as flat
rails, and to run cars thereon, to be propelled by horses or mules, and to carry
passengers thereon, as follows: Commencing at the intersection of the east
boundary of Main street with First street, and running thence east on First
street to Vignes street; thence northerly on Vignes street to Lazard street;
thence east on Lazard street to Center street, and thence north on Center street
to Aliso street, with all the necessary turnouts and switches of said Central
Railway Company, to depots located on said streets or terminus.

PROVIDED, FURTHER, and upon condition that the said grautee or its assigns
shall plank or pave the entire route along which said road may be constructed
between the rails, and for two feet on each side thereof, at all times whenever
ordered to do so by the Council of the City of Los Angeles, or by that body,
person or persons who may, by operation of law, succeed to the rights, duties or
privileges of the Council of the City of Los Angeles, and shall keep the same,
and all tracks and all portions of said streets over which any part of said track may
be constructed, between the rails, and for two feet on each side thereof, con-

stantly in repair, flush with the streets, and provided with good crossings for all
kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary and proper flumes and culverts for the
free and uninterrupted passage of the water under said track, from lands higher
than said track or roadbed is required to be, whenever and wherever the Council
of Los Angeles City, or the successor of said Council, shall order the said flumes
and culverts to be placed, and the track to be not more than five feet wide between
the rails, and there be a space between the main track and the side track or
turnouts sufficient to allow the cars to pass each other freely and without danger.

ProyiveD, FURTHER, that all curves made in the construction of this road
shall be designated and laid out by the City Surveyor of the City of Los Angeles ;
and PROVIDED, FURTHER, that the laying of said track shall conform, in all cases
where any grade has been established, to such established grades, and in all
other cases, to the natural grade of the street through which it may run, and
when at any time any part of said route shall be graded, or the grade thereof
changed or altered, the bed of the road and the track thereof shall be made by
the said Central Railway Company, its successors in interest and assigns, to
conform therewith ; provipED, and upon condition that the construction of said
road shall be commenced within six months from and after the date of the
taking effect of this ordinance, and the whole thereof shall be completed and
in running order within nine months from and after the date of the taking effect
of this ordinance.

Sec. 2. That whenever any other track shall intersect the road constructed
by virtue of this franchise, the owner of such intersecting track in no case shall
occupy or use a track of this road for a distance of more than five blocks, and
if the owners of such intersecting tracks cannot agree upon the amount of com-
pensation to be made therefor, the same may be ascertained and determined, as
provided in Title VII, Part III, Code of Civil Procedure, with amendments
thereto.

Sec. 3. Pxrovipep, FurTHER, and upon condition that at no time shall the
rate of fare for any distance along said road, and along those street railroads
constructed in pursuance and by virtue of the franchise granted by this ordi-
nance, of the franchise granted to Wm. H. Workman and A. H. Judson, by
ordinance approved June 26, 1875, the franchise granted to the Los Angeles
and Aliso Avenue Street Railroad Company, by ordinance approved February
3, 1887, and the franchise granted to the Central Railway Company, by ordi-
nance approved December 19, 1883, exceed the sum of five cents.

Sec. 4. That the owner or owners of said road shall pay, on the first Mon-
day of December of each year, a license to the City of Los Angeles upon each
car belonging to, or used by said Central Railway Company, of such an amount
as may be required by ordinance of said city.

Sec. 5. And provided that the laying down of the tracks of the said road
shall in all respects conform to the grade of said streets, established and regu-

===== PDF PAGE 014 =====
8 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

lated by said city, which said grade is to be designated by the City Surveyor to
the engineer of the road at the time of laying down the tracks, but subject to
the reservations, provisions and conditions herein contained.

Sec. 6. That this city in making the grant of this franchise reserves the
right to grade, renew, sewer, pave, macadamize, improve, alter or repair any of
said streets or any part thereof throughout the whole length of said road, and to lay
down pipes for water, gas and other purposes therein, such work to be done by
the city so as to obstruct the railroad as little as possible, and when work, or
the need for work, makes the same necessary, the owner or owners of said road
must shift the rails so as to avoid the obstructions made thereby. And, pro-
vided further, that this franchise is especially granted upon all and each of the
provisions, provisos and conditions herein contained and reserved, and if the
said grantee, or its successors or assigns, shall fail in any particular to comply
therewith, or with any one or more of them, or shall fail for the period of six
months or longer to operate, maintain or use the street railroad, or any part
thereof built by virtue of this franchise, all rights to all those portions of said
streets on which the said parts of said street railroad shall not have been used,
maintained or operated for the period of six months shall be thereby forfeited,
and this grant to that extent shall be null and void. And provided, further,
that nothing herein contained shall be construed as granting any exclusive
franchise in said streets, and all turn-tables are prohibited.

Sec. 7. All ordinances in conflict with this ordinance are hereby repealed.

Sec. 8. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heracp, aud thereupon this ordinance shall take effect and befin force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was.adopted by the Council of

ORDINANCE No. 118.

Aw Orpivance of the City of Los Angeles providing for the construction and
repairing of sidewalks on certain streets.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Whenever any portion of any street, lane, alley, court or place
in said city, improved, or any sidewalk constructed thereon according to law,
shall be out of repair and in condition to endanger persons or property passing
thereon, or in condition to interfere with the public convenience in the use
thereof, it shall be the duty of the Superintendent of Streets to require by
notice in writing, to be delivered to them personally or left on the premises, the
owners or occupants of lots, or portion of lots, fronting on said portion of said
street, lane, alley, court or place, or of said portion of said walk so out of
repair as aforesaid, to repair forthwith said portion of said street, lane, alley,
court or place to the center thereof or said sidewalk in front of the property of
which he is the owner, or tenant, or occupant, and said Superintendent of
Streets shall specify in said notice what repairs are required to be made. After

===== PDF PAGE 020 =====
14 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

the expiration of three days from the date of the service of said notice, the said
Superintendent of Streets shall be deemed to have acquired jurisdiction to con-
tract for the making of repairs required by said notice. If said repairs be not
commenced within three days after notice given as aforesaid and diligently and
without interruption prosecuted to completion, the said Superintendent of
Streets may, under authority from said City Council, make such repairs or enter
into a contract with any suitable person at the expense of the owner, tenant or
occupant at a reasonable price, to be determined by said Superintendent of
Streets, and such owner, tenant or occupant shall be liable to pay the same
upon the completion of said repairs by said contractor, as aforesaid, to the sat-
isfaction of said Superintendent of Streets; said Superintendent of Streets shall
make and deliver to said contractor a certificate to the effect that said repairs
have been properly made by said contractor, and the charges for the same are
reasonable and just, and that he, said Superintendent, has accepted the same.

Sec. 2. That hereafter all sidewalks, and the repairs of all sidewalks, of
such portions of the following named streets of said city as are hereinafter
described, shall be made and constructed’ of flat, smooth, even stone, either
natural or artificial, Schillinger’s patent stone, asphaltum, or in the following
manner: First, a layer of brick shall be placed, covering the entire sidewalk
to be constructed or repaired; then upon the top of the said layer of brick shall
be placed a mixture of brea and sand in the proportion of one-half of each in-
gredient, to a depth of at least one and one-half inches, rolled smooth, and
finally, a layer of sand on the top of all and not otherwise than as above stated.
The streets and portions of streets are:

On both sides of Main street, from the north line of Fourth street to a point
on Main street north of the Pico House and opposite the center of the Plaza.

On both sides of Spring street, from the north line of Fourth street to the
south line of Temple street. ¢

On both sides of Los Angeles street, from the north side of First street to
the south side of Arcadia street.

On both sides of First street, between Los Angeles street and Fort street.

On both sides of Requena street, between Main street and Wilmington
street.

On both sides of Commercial street, between Main street and Alameda
street.

On both sides of Arcadia street, between Main street and Los Angeles
street.

On both sides of Aliso street, between Los Angeles street and Alameda
street.

On both sides of Temple street, from Spring street to Buena Vista street.

On both sides of Upper Main street, between the Plaza and Virgin street,

On both sides of Sonora street, between Main street and New High street,

On both sides of Court street, between Main street and Spring street.

On both sides of Market street, between Main street and Spring street.

===== PDF PAGE 021 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 15

Sec. 3. All sidewalks. upon streets, or parts of streets, other than those
mentioned in Section two (2) of this ordinance, shall be constructed and repaired
by being filled to the established grade with fine, sharp gravel, properly leveled,
and no part of the gravel, in any case, shall exceed one inch in diameter, and
all stones one inch or more in diameter on said sidewalks shall be removed
therefrom, or broken into a size not exceeding one inch in diameter before
such filling, and all brush and weeds shall be removed before such filling.

Sec. 4. For every neglect to comply with the terms of this ordinance, the
owner of the said property shall forfeit and pay to the City of Los Angeles the
sum of fifty dollars, and the further penalty of ten dollars for each day during
which such neglect continues, to be recovered from the owner or owners of said
property.

Sec. 5. Any one violating the provisions of this ordinance, and any one
failing to repair or construct sidewalks after due notice given, within the time
and in the manner specified in the notice therefor, as hereinbefore provided,
shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and be fined not less than ten dollars nor
more than fifty dollars, or be imprisoned not less than ten days nor more than
fifty days in the city jail, and every additional day during which any person
shall fail to repair or construct sidewalks after due notice given, within the
time and in the manner specified in the notice therefor, as hereinbefore pro-
vided, shall constitute an additional offense, and shall be punishable as herein
specified. ;

Sec. 6. All ordinances and parts of ordinances, and all resolutions and
parts of resolutions, so far as they conflict with this ordinance, and no farther,
are hereby repealed.

Sec. 7. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HERALD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council
of the City of Los Angeles, at its regular meeting of February 11, 1884.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 11th day of February, A. D. 1884.

C. E. THOM,

Mayor.

An Orprnance establishing water rates and fixing the compensation for

water to be furnished by any person, company, or corporation for family
uses, for private purposes, for municipal uses, and for all public purposes in
the City of Los Angeles, for the year commencing July 1, 1884.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows :

Sxetron 1. The monthly rates of compensation to be collected by any
person, company, or corporation, engaged in the business of supplying water to
the inhabitants of the City of Los Angeles for domestic purposes, for private
purposes, for municipal purposes, and for all public purposes of said city for the
year commencing July 1, 1884, and ending June 30, 1885, are hereby fixed as
follows:

For tenements (including for bath-tub) occupied by a single family, for one-
story buildings, $1.50; for two-story buildings, $2; for three-story buildings,
$2.50.

Horses kept for private use, including water for washing one vehicle, for
each horse, 25 cents, and for each additional horse, 1244 cents, and for each ad-
ditional vehicle, 1214 cents.

For hose for washing windows, sidewalks, gardens, or grounds, for every
lot not more than sixty feet front, 50 cents; sixty to one hundred feet front, $1;
over one hundred feet front, two cents per front foot for all over one hundred
feet, in addition to the rate for the one hundred feet.

For each water-closet used in private houses, 25 cents.

For each water-closet used in public buildings, $2.

For each urinal used in private buildings, 25 cents.

for each urinal used in public buildings, $1.

Yor water furnished for building purposes, for each barrel of lime used, 20
cents.

For bakeries, for each barrel of flour, 5 cents.

Storés, banks, offices, warehouses, saloons, groceries, barber shops, butcher
shops, blacksmith shops, book-binderies, confectioners, churches, halls, laund-
ries, photograph galleries, printing offices, steam engines, greenhouses, markets,
market stores, horse troughs, soda fountains, and other places of business not
supplied by meter, to be charged according to the estimated quantity used, from
$1 to $10.

* When meters are used, then, if the quantity does not exceed 10,000 gallons
per month, for each 1,000 gallons, $1; over 10,000 gallons per month, 75 cents
for each 1,000 gallons.

Hotels, taverns, boarding-houses, boarding-schools, lodging- houses, in addi-
tion to family rates, for each hoarder or lodger, 10 cents.

For every bath-tub used in barber shops, bathing establishments and hotels,
$2.50.

===== PDF PAGE 023 =====
OF THE GITY OF LOS ANGELES. 17

Fountains shall be regulated by contract.

All persons, companies, or corporations, furnishing water as aforesaid
shall have power in all cases to apply meters, at their own expense, for the
purpose of discovering waste or excessive use, and when waste or excessive use
is found, to charge meter rates.

For water required for purposes that are not specified in the above tariff, the
rates shall be in proportion to the above tariff when meters are not used, and
the meter rates when meters are used.

All water furnished for sprinkling streets, flushing sewers, watering parks,
or water used for the extinguishment of fires, shall be furnished free ; provided,
that when the City of Los Angeles is not entitled by law or contract to water

All rates, except meter rates, are due and payable in advance, and meter
rates are due and payable at the end of the month, and upon meter rates a de-
posit not exceeding three-fourths (34) of the value of the estimated quantity of
water to be consumed for the month may be required.

ORDINANCE No. 121.

An Orprnance fixing the price of water for irrigatmg purposes.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows :

Section 1. The price of water for irrigating purposes shall, until and in-
cluding the 31st day of May, 1884, be as follows:

For one day, $2 per head.

For one-half day, $1.25 per head.

For one hour, 50 cents per head.

For one night, $1.25 per head

Sec. 2. If at any time there shall be a surplus of water unsold, the Zan-
jero is hereby authorized to rent the use of the city ditches through which to
carry water to persons residing outside the limits of the city until and including
the 31st day of May, 1884, for the following prices, to-wit:

For one day, $4 per head.

For one night, $2 per head.

Section 3. The price of water for irrigating purposes shall, on and after
June Ist, 1854, be as follows:

For one day, $3 per head.

For one-half day, $1.75 per head.

For'one hour, $1 per head.

For one night, $1.75 per head.

Sec. 4. If at any time there shall be a surplus of water unsold, the Zan-
jero is hereby authorized to rent the use of the city ditches through which to
carry water to persons residing outside the limits of the city on and after June
1, 1884, for the following prices, to-wit :

For one day, $6 per head.

For one night, $3 per head.

Sec. 5. Nothing herein contained shall be construed as a relinquishment
on the part of the city to fully control the disposition of the use of the waters
of the Los Angeles river for irrigating purposes, and the time of the hour

water shall be at the discretion of the Zanjero, and one day shall be from sun- .
rise to sunset, and one night shall be from sunset to sunrise.

Sec. 6. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

Sec. 7. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HeraLp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

sidewalks and the construction of sewers within municipalities,” approved
March 6, 1883; shall superintend and direct the chain-gang of the City of Los
Angeles, and all laborers and workinen performing any work or labor upon all
sewers, pipes, water pipes, streets, sidewalks, lanes, alleys, crosswalks, gutters,
parks, plazas, lands and property of the City of Los Angeles, and the Los
Angeles river and river-bed ; shall keep all streets, lanes, alleys, pavements and
gutters in repair and free from obstructions, and cause adjoining property owners
and holders to keep the same in repair; shall co-operate with and assist the
Health Officer in keeping the City of Los Angeles free and clear of all nuis-
ances, and shall perform such other duties as the Council of the City of Los
Angeles shall from time to time impose.

Sec. 2. The Superintendent of Streets shall, subject to the orders of said

Council, have control of the chaingang and all laborers performing work in all
places enumerated in section 1 of this ordinance.

E Sec. 3. The Superintendent of Streets shall report to the Council at each

expenditures made since his last report.

ORDINANCE No. 123.

An OrprNance regulating the keeping and the serving of stallions, jacks, bulls,
boars and dogs.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any one in the limits of the City of Los
Angeles to keep or let to a mare any stallion or jack, or to keep or let toa
cow any bull, or to let to a sow any boar, or to let to a bitch any dog, unless
such person shall provide an enclosure, so arranged as to entirely obstruct the
view thereof from all individuals.

Sec. 2. Any person violating any provision of this ordinance shall be
guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on conviction, be punished by a fine of not
less than ten nor more than two hundred dollars, or by imprisonment in the
city jail not less than ten nor more than one hundred and fifty days, or by both
such fine and imprisonment.

ORDINANCE No, 131.

An Orprvance for the prevention of vagrancy within the limits of the City of
Los Angeles, County of Los Angeles, State of California.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows :

Section 1. Every person (except a California Indian) without visible means
of living, who has the physical ability to work, and who does not for the space
of ten days seek employment, nor labor when employment is offered him ; every
healthy beggar who solicits alms as a business, every person who roams about
from place to place, without any lawful business, every idle or dissolute person,
or associate of known thieves, who wanders about the streets at late or unusual
hours of the night, or who lodges in any barn, shed, shop, outhouse, vessel or
place other than such as is kept for lodging purposes, without permission of the
owner or party entitled to the posession thereof, every lewd and dissolute person,
who lives in and about houses of ill-fame, and every common prostitute and
common drunkard is hereby declared a vagrant.

bec. 2. It is hereby declared unlawful for any vagrant, specified in section
one (1) of this ordinance, to come or live within the limits of the City of Los
Angeles.

Sec. 3. Any one violating the provisions of this ordinance shall, on con-
viction thereof, be punished by a fine of not exceeding ninety dollars, and, in
default of payment thereof, shall be imprisoned in the city jail of Los Angeles
City until the fine is satisfied, in the proportion of one day’s imprisonment for
every dollar of the fine.

===== PDF PAGE 038 =====
32 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 4. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

Src. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heratp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of July 29, A. D, 1884.

W. W. ROBINSON.
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 30th day of July, A. D. 1884.

C. E. THOM,

ORDINANCE No. 182.

An OrDINANCE suppressing and prohibiting games of chance and gambling
houses within the limits of the City of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Srction 1. The game of faro, monte, roulette, /ausgueuette, rouge et noir,
rondo or any banking game, or any game played with cards, dice, or any other
device for money, checks, credit, or any other representative of value, are
hereby declared to be, and the same are games of chance.

Src. 2. All persons are hereby prohibited from attending, or being present
in any room or rooms where any game of chance, played with cards, dice or
other device for money, checks, credit or other representative of value is being
played, conducted or carried on, under a penalty, on conviction, of a fine not
exceeding fifty dollars.

Sec. 3. Any room or rooms within the limits of the City of Los Angeles,
wherein either the game of faro, monte, roulette, lansquenette, rouge et noir, or
rondo is played, conducted or carried on with cards, dice, or any other device for

money, checks, credit, or any other representative of value, is hereby declared
to be, and the same is a gambling house.

Sec. 4. All persons are hereby prohibited from attending or being present
in any gambling house within the limits of the City of Los Angeles, under a
penalty, on conyiction, of a fine not exceeding fifty dollars.

===== PDF PAGE 039 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. go

This section shall not apply to officers of the law in discharge of their
duties.

Sec. 5. Any person who shall keep any room, building, arbor, booth, shed
or tenement, to be used or occupied for gambling, or as a gambling house,
or if the owner, superintendent or agent of any room, building, arbor, booth,
shed or tenement shall rent, or permit the same to be used or occupied for
gambling, or a gambling house, or, after having rented, or permitted any room,
building, arbor, booth, shed or tenement, or other premises, he shall become
aware that the same is used or occupied for gambling, or a gambling house, and
shall fail, within a reasonable time after having obtained such knowledge, to
report the same to the Judge of the City Court, or Chief of Police of Los
Angeles City, he shall, on conviction* be fined not exceeding three hundred
dollars.

Sec. 6. Every owner or lessee, or keepr of any house used, in whole or in
part as a saloon or drinking place, who knowingly permits any person under
twenty-one years of age to play at any game of chance therein, is guilty of a
misdemeanor, and shall be fined not exceeding one hundred dollars.

Sec. 7. If any person for gambling purposes shall keep or exhibit any
gambling table, establishment, device or apparatus, or if any person or persons
shall act as a lookout or gamekeeper for the games of monte, faro, or any other
banking game or games of chance where money or property is dependent on the
result, he shall, on conviction, be fined not exceeding two hundred dollars.

Sec. 8. It shall be the duty of the police of said city to seize and safely
keep all chips, checks, cards, boxes, tables, boards and all other articles used or
pertaining to the games of faro, monte, roulette, lansquenette, rouge et noir,
rondo or any banking games played with cards, dice or any other device for
money, checks, credit or other representative of value, and produce the same
in court and to be retained until the final disposition of any case in which said
articles may be required as evidence, to be then destroyed by the order of the
Judge of the City Court, but nothing herein contained shall prevent the destruc-
tion of said articles at any time when the Judge of said court may deem said
articles no longer required to be retained for evidence.

Sec. 9. Every person duly summoned as a witness for the prosecution, or
any proceedings had under this ordinance, who neglects or refuses to attend as
required shall, on conviction, be punished by fine not exceeding one hundred
dollars.

Sec. 10 It is hereby provided that all prosecutions under this ordinance
shall be in the City Court of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 11. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon it shall take effect and be in force.

ORDINANCE No. 135.
An ORDINANCE tegulating the registry of dogs.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. No dog, or slut or bitch shall run at large in the City of Los
Angeles unless the owner thereof shall strap upon the neck of such dog, or slut
or bitch a collar made of some durable substance on which the tag hereinafter
described shall be kept, and unless such owner shall give his name and a
description of such dog, or slut or bitch to the pound-keeper of said city, who
shall register with a proper number the same in a book to be kept by him for
that purpose, with a number corresponding with the register of such dog, or
slut or bitch, and at the same time the ownershall pay to the said pound-keeper,
for his own use, the sum of one dollar ($1) for each and every dog and
three dollars ($3) for each and every slut or bitch kept and owned by him
and suffered to run at large, which shall be in full for license for one year from
the 15th day of August, 1884, until the 14th day of August, 1885, and thereafter
pay alike tax on such dog, or slut or bitch for each year thereafter. Pro-
vided, that upon said payment the said pound-keeper shall deliver to the person
so paying a tag containing an appropriate number, which tag shall be good
until the succeeding August 14th; and provided, further, that a year within the
meaning of this ordinance commences on August 15th and ends on August 14th
of every calender year.

===== PDF PAGE 044 =====
38 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 2. Every dog, or slut or bitch found running at large contrary to the
provisions of section 1 of this ordinance shall be deemed a nuisance, and it
shall be the duty of the pound-keeper to, at all times, enforce this ordinance,
and for and in consideration of the moneys that may be paid to him under the
provisions of section 1 hereof the said pound-keeper shall take up any such dog,
or slut or bitch and advertise the same for five (5) days by written notice at the
office of the Chief of Police of said city, and shall keep such dog, or slut or bitch
in some safe place for that space of time, which place shall be made known in
said notice, and in order to obtain any such dog, or slut or bitch the owner
thereof shall pay to said pound-keeper two ($2) dollars for each dog and six
dollars ($6) for each slut or bitch, and upon said payment a tag for said dog, or
slut or bitch shall be issued to the owner thereof, in the same manner as pro-
vided in section one of this ordinance, which tag shall be good until the 14th
of the succeeding August, and if no owner thereof shall appear and claim said
dog, or slut or bitch, within the said five days from the said date of taking up, it
shall be the duty of the said pound-keeper to kill the said animal and remove
the same. ;

Sec. 3. If any slut or bitch be found running at large, within the limits of
said city, during the period of her heat, the same shall be considered a public
nuisance, and at once killed by the said pound-keeper, any person designated by
him, or any police officer.

Sec. 4. If any person shall attempt to prevent any one of said persons
from performing any act hereinbefore prescribed by them to be done, he shall
be guilty of a misdemeaner, and shall, on conviction, be fined in a sum not less
than ten dollars nor more than three hundred dollars, or be imprisoned in the
city jail not less than ten days and not more than three months, or be both so
fined and imprisoned.

Sec. 5. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

Sec. 6. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, rnd thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of August 12, 1884.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.
Approved this 13th day of August, 1884.

C. E. THOM,

For one night, two dollars.

For one day, one dollar.
For one night, fifty cents.

jero is hereby authorized to rent the use of the city ditches through which to
carry water to persons residing outside the limits of the city for the following
prices after the month of October, 1884, and commencing November 1, 1884,

An Orprnance of the City of Los Angeles granting to §. K. Sewall and his

streets of said city for a period of ten years.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. 8. K. Sewall and his assigns are hereby granted for the period
of ten years from the date of the passage and approval of this ordinance, the
right and are hereby authorized to erect and maintain telephone poles upon,
and to run wires over and along the public streets and thoroughfares within
the limits of the City of Los Angeles, under the provisions of sections two and

three of this ordinance.

Sec. 2. Such poles so erected and to be erected shall be placed fifty yards
apart, unless otherwise ordered by the Council of said city, or by the snecessors
in interest and rights of said Council, and shall in all cases set in the curb, and
shall not project more than two inches into the gutter where streets are side-
walked, when not otherwise directed by said Council or its said successors, and
upon all other streets and thoroughfares at such points as may be designated
by said Council or its said successors. The Council of the City of Los Angeles and
its said successors shall have supervision over the location under this ordinance

===== PDF PAGE 063 =====
 

s OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 57

of all poles to be erected by said Sewall or his assigns; said Council, for itself
and successors, reserve the right to remove or cause to be removed any of the
poles or wires of said Sewall or his assigns whenever the public convenience
shall require the location of the same elsewhere. In no case shall any wire of
said Sewall or his assigns be lower than 18 feet from the ground, and the said
wires shall be entirely above or below the other telephone and telegraph wires
in said city. The exchange of said telephone system shall be in working order
within 120 days from the taking effect of this ordinance.

Sec. 3. Said Sewall and his assigns shall give, during all of said period of
ten years, free of charge, to the City of Los Angeles the use of all their telephone
lines and wires, within the limits of said city, for the Police Department, Fire
Department, Council, and the successors of the Council of said city, and shall ©
immediately place, and during all of said period of ten years shall maintain an
instrument for sending and receiving telephone messages—the said instrument
having the same connection with the central office and all other portions of
said telephone lines as other operating telephone instruments of said Sewall
and his assigns shall hayve—in the room which the said Council or its successors
shall occupy for their place of meeting, in the office of the Chief of Police of
said city and in every room in which any fire-engine, hose-cart or hook and
ladder truck belonging to said city shall be stationed.

Src. 4. This franchise is granted upon each and every condition contained
in this ordinance; and upon the failure or refusal of said Sewall or his assigns
to comply with any one or more of the conditions of this ordinance this fran-
chise shall at once cease and determine, and the said Sewall and his assigns
shall have no rights whatever by virtue of this ordinance.

Src. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herap, a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter it
shall take effect and be in force.

T hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of December 9, A. D. 1884.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Aw Orpinance establishing water rates and fixing the compensation for water
to be furnished by any person, company or corporation for family uses, for
private purposes, for municipal uses and for all public purposes in the city
of Los Angeles, for the year commencing July 1, 1885.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. The monthly rates of compensation to be collected by any
person, company or corporation engaged in the business of supplying water to
the inhabitants of the City of Los Angeles for domestic purposes, for private
purposes, for municipal purposes and for all public purposes of said city for the

pp Te eeroner anc Crist Company

year commencing July 1, 1885, and ending June 30, 1886, are hereby fixed as
follows:

For tenements, including bath tub, occupied by single family—for one-
story buildings, one dollar and fifty cents; for two-story buildings, two dollars ;
for three-story buildings, two dollars and fifty cents.

Horses kept for private use, including water for washing one vehicle, for
one horse, twenty-five cents; for each additional horse, twelve and one-half
cents; for each additional vehicle, twelve and one-half cents.

For hose for washing windows, sidewalks, gardens or grounds, for every
lot not more than sixty feet front, fifty cents; sixty toone hundred feet front,
one dollar; over one hundred feet front, two cents per front foot for all over one
hundred feet front in addition to the rate for the one hundred feet.

For each water closet used in private house, twenty-five cents.

For each water closet used in public buildings, two dollars.

For each urinal used in private buildings, twenty-five cents.

For each urinal used in public buildings, one dollar.

For water furnished for building purposes for each barrel of lime used,
twenty cents. .

For bakeries, for each barrel of flour, five cents.

Stores, banks, offices, warehouses, saloons, groceries, barber shops, butcher
shops, blacksmith shops, book binderies, confectioners, churches, halls, laun-
dries, photograph galleries, printing offices, steam engines, greenhouses, markets,

When meters are used, if the quantity used does not exceed ten thousand
gallons per month, for each one thousand gallons, one dollar; if over ten |
thousand gallons per month, seventy-five cents for each one thousand.gallons.

Hotels, taverns, boarding-houses, boarding-schools, lodging-houses, in
addition to family rates, for each boarder or lodger, ten cents.

For every bath tub used in barber shops, bathing establishments and hotels,
two dollars and fifty cents.

Fountains shall be regulated by contract.

| All persons, companies or corporations furnishing water as aforesaid, shall
have power in all cases to apply meters, at their own expense, for the purpose
of discovering waste or excessive use, and when waste or excessive use is

. found to charge meter rates.

For water required for purposes that are not specified in the above tariff, the
rates shall be in proportion to the above tariff when meters are not used, and
the meter rates when meters are used. ;

ORDINANCE No, 158.

An Orprance prohibiting the placing of building materials in the streets of
the City of Los Angeles without the consent of the Council, and making
certain regulations in regard to such obstructions.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person, persons or corporation to
obstruct any street of the City of Los Angeles by placing building material
therein, or otherwise, except by consent of the Council of said city, previously
obtained, and unless a deposit of twenty-five dollars has been made with the
Superintendent of Streets of said city; provided, that in no case shall any part
of a street be obstructed to a greater distance than twenty feet from the sidewalk
adjoining the building for which the said material is intended.

Sec. 2. Consent of Council having been obtained, and the required de-
posit having been made, any person placing materials for building in the street
must proceed with the construction of the building for which the material is

. erie
om.
-_ en

:
ree, £m

===== PDF PAGE 073 =====
 

7
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 67

intended. as rapidly as the weather and obtainable supply of workmen and
material will permit, and remove the said material and debris thereof with all
possible dispatch.

Sec. 3. Any person or persons, or corporation, placing or causing to be
placed any building materials in said streets, shall swing two lighted lanterns
upon said material, one at each end thereof, and two feet from the ground, and

arranged soas to keep burning from half an hour after sunset until half an
hour before sunrise of each day.

Sec. 3. If every portion of the said building material, and the debris
thereof, shall not have been removed within three days after the completion of
said building, it shall be the duty of the Superintendent of Streets of the City
of Los Angeles to cause the removal of the said materials and debris, and pay
the expense of the removal thereof out of said deposit in his hands.

Sec. 4. After all of said materials and debris has been removed, the
Superintendent of Streets shall pay to the person entitled thereto the balance

of the said twenty-five dollars remaining after paying the expenses of removal
of said materials and debris.

Sec. 5. Any person or persons, firm or corporation violating any of the
provisions of this ordinance shall, upon conviction, pay a fine of not more than
two hundred and fifty dollars, or be imprisoned not more than two hundred and
fifty days, or both pay said fine and suffer said imprisonment. Each day’s con-
tinuance of such violation shall be regarded as a separate offence.

Sec. 6. All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

Sec. 7. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herap, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of February 26, 1885.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 28th day of February, 1885.

E. F. SPENCE,

and constructing, laying down, maintaining and operating a double track cable
street railroad, with iron or steel rails and running cars thereon—that is to Say :

Commencing at the intersection of Second street with the westerly line of
Spring street, and running thence westerly along said Second street on each
side of the center line thereof, to Lake Shore avenue; thence westerly along
said Lake Shore avenue on each side of the center line thereof to Diamond
street; thence westerly along said Diamond street on each side of center line
thereof to the west boundary of said city.

Provided, and upon condition that the said grantee or his assigns shall
plank, pave or macadamize the entire length of said route along which said
road may be constructed between the rails and for two feet on each side thereof,
and shall keep the same constantly in repair, flush with the grades of the
streets and provide with good crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all
necessary and proper flumes and culverts for the free and uninterrupted passage
of water under said tracks, from lands higher than said tracks or roadbeds, is
required to be, and the tracks be not more than three and a half feet between
the rails, and that the rails be well guarded with planks and stringers, and
there be sufficient space between the tracks and each of the tracks and side
tracks, or turnouts, to allow the cars to pass each other freely and without
danger ; and provided, further, that the laying of said tracks, except as herein-
after provided, shall conform in all cases, when any grade has been established,
to such established grade, and in all other cases to the natural grade of the
street through which they may run, and when at any time any part of said
route shall be graded, or the grade thereof changed or altered, the bed of the
road and the tracks thereof shall be made to conform therewith.

Provided, that the said grantee or his assigns may construct said road from
the west boundary of Bunker Hill avenue to the west boundary of Hope street
on a vertical alignment conforming to the established grade at said west
boundary of Hope street and said west boundary of Bunker Hill avenue, said
proviso being made under the express 'condition that said grantee or his adsigns
shall provide a suitable crossing at the intersection of Hope street and Second

===== PDF PAGE 076 =====
70 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

street, said crossing to be 40 feet in width, and adjoining the west boundary of
Hope street, on the west side thereof, and to be constructed whenever Hope
street shall be graded.

Provided, that the said grantee or his assfgns may construct a wooden trestle
from a point on Second street about 40 feet east of Hope street to a point about
70 feet east of Flower street upon which to erect said cable railway, said proviso
last above named being under the express condition that said grantee, or his
assigns, shall grade the section of Second street along which said trestle shall
extend and be constructed to a level with and flush with the top of the rails of
said cable railway, by constructing thereon an earthen embankment extending
the entire length of said trestle, said embankment to have a cross sectional
width of 16 feet at its top, with lateral slopes of one and one-half feet horizontal
to one foot vertical.

Provided, that no turnout or switch shall be constructed, except in places
designated by the Council of the City of Los Angeles, nor shall such turnout in
any case be nearer than twenty-five feet to the junction of any two streets, or
the intersection of any cross streets. Provided, further, that the rate of fare
for any distance along said road shall at no time exceed five cents for one
passenger, and the owner or owners of said road shall pay to the city of Los
Angeles such license for each car as may be required by the ordinances of said
city. No Chinese labor shall be employed in the construction or operating of
said road.

Sec. 2. It is understood that the grant of this franchise gives to the
grantee or his assigns the right to excavate for and construct, lay down and
maintain a single line of track over and along said route, and operate the same
until he or his assigns may deem it necessary or expedient to construct, lay
down and maintain a double track as aforesaid; and it is further understood
that the grant of this right carries with it the right to construct, erect, lay
down and maintain such engine-houses, engines, boilers, machinery, turnouts
and switches as may be necessary or proper for the operation of said road. —

It is further understood that the city, in making the grant of this franchise,
expressly reserves the right to grade, renew, sewer, pave, macadamize, improve,
alter or repair all or either of said streets, or any part thereof, and to lay down
pipes for water, gas and other purposes—such work to be done by the city, so
as to obstruct or injure said road as little as possible, but when such work
makes the same necessary, the owner or owners of said road must shift the rails
so as to avoid the obstruction made thereby.

Sec. 3. The above rights and privileges are granted upon the express con-
dition that the said road shall be fully completed, equipped, stocked and in
running order, from the westerly line of Spring street to the easterly line of
Texas street, within the period of one year from the passage of this ordinance,
and the entire road shall be completed within three years from the passage of

be thereby forfeited, and this grant shall be null and void.

ORDINANCE No. 162.

Aw Orpinance forbidding the carrying on of business or work of laundries
between certain hours.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1, The keeping open of any laundry or wash house, or carrying
on of work in the same within the limits of the City of Los Angeles, between
the hours of nine and a half in the evening and five in the morning, is hereby
declared to be a nuisance, and it shall be unlawful for any person, either as
owner, agent or employe, to conduct or carry on, or assist in carrying on, the
business or work of any laundry or wash house between the hours above
named.

ORDINANCE No. 163.

Ax Orprxance forbidding the hanging of meat, or bodies of slaughtered
animals, over public sidewalks.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to place or hang
over or upon any of the public sidewalks or streets of the City of Los Angeles

any meat, beef, mutton, pork, game, poultry, fish, body or part of body of any
slaughtered animal.

Sec. 2. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to place, or cause
to be placed, keep or maintain upon any public street of the City of Los
Angeles any iron hook, spike or nail, pointing toward the sidewalk of said
street ; and the Chief of Police is hereby directed and authorized to notify all
persons having such hooks, spikes or nails in front of their places of business
to have the same immediately removed.

Sec. 3. Any person or persons who shall violate the provisions of this
ordinance shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction
thereof, shall be punished by fine of not more than one hundred dollars, or by

imprisonment for not more than one hundred days, or by both such fine and
imprisonment.

all other cases to the natural grade of the streets through which they may be
constructed; and when at any time any part of said route shall be graded, or
the grade thereof changed or altered, the bed of the road, and the tracks
thereof shall be made to conform therewith.

Provided, further, and upon condition that at no time shall the rate of fare
for any distance along said road and the road known as the City Railroad,
owned by the City Railroad Company, exceed the sum of five cents for one

through fare.

Provided, further, and upon condition, that if at any time for the space of
six months the said road, or any portion thereof, be unused by said Hellman or
his assigns, as a street railroad, the franchise for the said portion so unused
shall be thereby forfeited.

Provided, further, and upon condition that the bridge crossing the Los
Angeles river shall consist of spans not less than sixty-four feet between centers
of piers, and to extend across the official bed of said river; provided, further,
and upon condition that no Chinese labor shall be employed in the construction
and operating of said road.

Src. 2. It is understood that the city expressly reserves the right to grade,
sewer, pave, macadamize, improve, alter, or repair all or either of said streets, or
any part thereof, throughout the whole length of said road; and to lay down
pipes for water, gas or other purposes; such work to be done by the city so as
to obstruct or injure the said road as little as possible; but, when work makes
the same necessary, the owner or owners of said road must shift the rails so as
to avoid the obstruction made thereby. ‘

It is further understood that this franchise is especially granted upon each
and all of the provisions and conditions herein contained and reserved, and if
said grantee, or his successors or assigns, shall fail in any particular to comply
therewith, or with either of them, then and in that case all rights to this fran-
chise shall be thereby forfeited, and this grant shall be null and void; and that
nothing herein contained shall be construed in any manner as granting an ex-
clusive franchise.

Src. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-

nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HERALD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council
of the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of June 9, 1885.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

ORDINANCE No. 175.

Aw Orprnance to provide for the issue of bonds for the purpose of making
certain necessary improvements.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Whereas the sum of two hundred and forty-five thousand dol-
lars is required by the City of Los Angeles for the purpose of making the im-
provements hereinafter specified ; and whereas, the Constitution of the State of
California provides that such indebtedness can be incurred only after the assent
of two-thirds of the qualified electors of the city voting at an election held for
that purpose, nor unless before or at the time of incurring such indebtedness
provision shall be made for the collection of an annual tax sufficient to pay the
interest on such indebtedness as it falls due, and also to constitute a sinkin,
fund for the payment of the principal thereof within twenty years from the
time of contracting the same; and whereas, the City of Los Angeles, subject

===== PDF PAGE 094 =====
88 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS :

to said limitation as contained in the Constitution, has the power to incur the
indebtedness amounting to two hundred and forty-five thousand dollars; there-
fore, be it ordained as follows: The City of Los Angeles shall issue the bonds
of said city to an amount not exceeding two hundred and forty-five thousand
dollars to be payable on er before the expiration of twenty years from the date
of their issue, with interest thereon at the rate of six per cent. per annum,
payable semi-annually on the first day of January and July in each year, both
principal and interest to be made payable in lawful money of the United States.
The bonds shall be issued in the denomination of five hundred dollars each,
and shall be signed by the Mayor of the City of Los Angeles and the Auditor
of said city. Interest coupons shall be attached to said bonds. signed by the
Auditor of the City of Los Angeles. The City Council shall provide for the
issue of said bonds at such time as shall be necessary to provide funds for the
' making of the improvements hereafter specified.

Sec. 2. The bonds and coupons shall be payable at the office of the City
Treasurer, and all coupons as soon as they are paid shall be detached and can-
celled by the City Treasurer, and by him, within one month thereafter,
deposited with the City Auditor, who shall give the Treasurer his receipt for
any such deposit of coupons. Every bond issued pursuant to this ordinance
shall bear the date of its issue, and upon the sale thereof the purchaser shall
pay in addition to the purchase price of said bond all accrued interest up to the
date of sale thereof.

Src. 3. The Council of the City of Los Aegeles shall hereafter make the
necessary regulations for the sale of said bonds, but no bond shall be sold for
less than its face value.

Sec. 4. Before the issue of said bonds the Mayor and Council of the City
of Los Angeles shall by ordinance make provision for the levy of a tax suffi-
cient to pay the interest upon the said bonds as the same shall fall due, and
for the establishment of a sinking fund for the payment of the principal when
the same shall become due and payable.

Sec. 5. The said bonds shall be known as the General Improvement
bonds of the City of Los Angeles, and the proceeds thereof shall be appro-
priated as follows: To the improvement of irrigation system, $120,000; to
construction of sewers, $40,000; to completion of City Hall, $65,000; to build-
ing and repairing bridges and street improvement, $20,000.

Sec. 6. At any time within one month after this ordinance shall have
gone into effect, the Council of the City of Los Angeles may by resolution call
a special election of the qualified electors of the City of Los Angeles for the
purpose of voting upon the question of the issue or non-issue of the bonds
hereinbefore provided for, in accordance with the provisions of section 18,
Article XI, of the Constitution of the State of California, which election shall
be called, held, conducted and declared in all respects as provided in Article X
of the Revised Charter of the City of Los Angeles.

ORDINANCE No. 176.

An Orprxance providing for the protection of the public streets of the City of
Los Angeles.

_ The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Any person or.persons digging up or excavating, or causing to
be excavated, any part of any public street of the City of Los Angeles, under
permission granted, or otherwise, shall, within ten days after the making of
such excavation, cause the same to be filled up, and the streets, sidewalk, eurb
or gutter fully and in every respect to be rsstored to its former condition, and
shall keep the said street, so far as affected by such excavation, in good repair
for thirty days from the time of filling up such excavation.

Sec. 2. Any person or corporation failing or neglecting in any particular
to comply with any provision of this ordinance shall be deemed guilty of a
misdemeanor. and, upon convictron thereof, shall be fined in a sum not less
than twenty-five dollars nor more than two hundred dollars, or be imprisoned not
more than ninety days, or suffer both such fine and imprisoment.

See. 3. This ordinance shall not be construed to affect in any way any
ordinance requiring persons to obtain permit before excavating or digging up
any public street, or any provision requiring a deposit before the grant of such
permit.

ORDINANCE No. 179.

An OrpINANCE requiring all milk wagons used in the City of Los Angeles to
be numbered.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1, Every milk wagon used for the sale of milk in the City of Los
Angeles shall have a number printed or painted thereon, or tacked thereto, in
plain Arabic figures, not less than one inch and a half in height and of pro-
portionate width, and of such color as to be readily distinguished. Such
number shall be designated by the Tax Collector.

Sec. 2. No person shall use or drive, or permit to be used or driven, any
milk wagon belonging to him or under his control without having the appro-
priate number placed thereon in a conspicuous place on each side, nor with
such number inverted, covered, mutilated, obliterated or obscurely painted or
illegible.

Sec. 3. Any person violating the provisions of this ordinance shall be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be pun-

ORDINANCE No. 180.

An Orprnance to provide for the employment of prisoners confined in city
jail.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. All persons confined in the city jail of the City of Los Angeles
under a judgment of imprisonment rendered in a criminal action for violation
of ordinances of the city, shall be required to perform labor on the public works
or ways of the city, under the direction of the Overseer of the Chain Gang.

Sec. 2, The Chief of Police shall cause as many of said prisoners as shall
be deemed necessary to be put in charge of the Overseer of the Chain Gang
each day, to perform such labor as the Superintendent of Streets may designate.

Sec. 3. The Overseer of the Chain Gang shall be sworn in as a special
policeman of the city, and a sufficient number of guards shall be employed for
the safe keeping of said prisoners, to enforce the performance of the work
assigned to them, and to prevent their escape.

Sec. 4. Any prisoner employed, as above directed, who escapes while so
employed, or while going to or returning from public work, shall be deemed guilty

of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction, shall be punished by imprisonment of
not less than ten nor more than fifty days.

Sec. 5. The Overseer of the Chain Gang shall procure and use such means

===== PDF PAGE 102 =====
96 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

as he shall deem necessary for the security of all prisoners under his charge,
and may prescribe and administer, or cause to be administered, such punish-
ment as shall be deemed necessary to keep good order among the prisoners,
and compel them to do their work.

Sec. 6. The Police Commissioner shall prescribe such further rules and
regulations as shall be necessary for the carrying into effect of this ordinance.

Sec. 7. The prisoners shall be treated with the utmost kindness, com-
patible with the enforcement of the rules and regulations necessary to compel
discipline and obedience to the officer in charge.

Src. 8. All ordinances and parts of ordinances inconsistant herewith are
hereby repealed.

Sec. 9. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herawp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of July 14, 1885.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 17th day of July, 1885.

E. F. SPENCE,
Mayor.

ORDINANCE No. 182.

An Orprnance to provide for the destruction of insects injurious to trees, fruit
or vegetation.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That all orchards, nurseries, vineyards, gardens, lawns, lands
or other places infected, or in which there exists the insect known as the white
cottony cushion scale, or scale bug, or other. insect injurious to fruits, fruit
trees, vines, shrubs, or other vegetation, be and the same are hereby declared
to be public nuisances.

Sec. 2. It shall be the duty of every owner or agent of property within
_ the City of Los Angeles infected by any such insect to immediately remove,
destroy and eradicate such insect and abate such nuisance.

Sec. 3. The offices of Inspectors of Fruit Pests of the City of -Los Angeles
are hereby created.

necessary excavations for and constructing, laying down, maintaining and ope-
rating a line of street railroad track, with its necessary turnouts and switches,
and running cars thereon, to be drawn or propelled by cable wire; that is to say:

Commencing at the intersection of Spring and First streets, thence running
east along First street to the southwest corner of the bridge that crosses the Los
Angeles river at First street ; thence across the Los Angeles river on a bridge to

Provided, further, that the said grantee or his assigns shall construct a good
and substantial bridge across the official bed of the Los Angeles river at First
street, using spans of not less than one hundred feet between center of piers.
The plans and specifications for the bridge across the Los Angeles river to be
subject to the approval of the city survey and the Council of the City of Los
Angeles.

Sec. 2. Provided and upon condition that the said grantee or his assigns
shall plank, pavesor macadamize the entire length of said route along which said
road may be constructed between the rails and for two feet on each side thereof,
whenever ordered to do so by the Council of the City of Los Angeles, when
any of said streets are being paved, planked or macadamized, and shall keep
the same constantly in repair, flush with the streets and provided with good
crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary and proper flumes and
culverts for the free and uninterrupted passage of water from rains, or other
drainage ; and provided, further, that the laving of said tracks shall conform in
all cases, when any grade has been established, to such established grade, and
in all other cases to the natnral grade of the street through which they may
run, and when at any time any part of said route shall be graded, or the
grade thereof changed or altered, the bed of the road and the tracks thereof
shall be made to conform therewith. And it is further understood that the grant
of this right carries with it the right to construct and maintain such switchings
and sidings as may be necessary or proper for the operation of said road.

Sec. 3. And it is further understood that the city, in making the grant of
this franchise, expressly reserves the right to grade, renew, sewer, pave, macada-
mize, improve, alter or repair all or either of said streets, or any part thereof,
and to lay down pipes for water, gas and other purposes-——such work to be done
by the city, so as to obstruct or injure said road as little as possible, but when
work makes the same necessary, the owner or owners of said road must shift the
rails so as to avoid the obstruction made thereby.

vision to the end that a good and substantial bridge may be built.

Sec. 4. The above rights and privileges are granted upon the express con-

’ ditions that the said road shall be commenced within three months from the

taking effect of this ordinance, and shall be fully completed, equipped, stocked

and in running order within the period of one year from the passage of this
ordinance.

It is further understood that this franchise is granted upon all and each of
the provisions and conditions herein contained, it being understood that this
franchise shall be forfeited by the grantee herein, or his assigns, on account of
failure to complete the said road within the said period of one year, only for
that portion of said road which at that time shall remain and be unfinished,
leaving the franchise for that portion of said road completed and in running
order unaffected by such failure.

Sec. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of August 25, 1885.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 7th day of September, 1885.

D. E. MILES,

ORDINANCE No. 191.

An Orprnance to provide for the suppressing and prohibiting of gaming with
cards, games of chance and gambling houses within the limits of the City
of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City 6f Los Angeles, do ordain as follows :

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to deal, play,
carry on, open, or cause to be opened or conducted, as either owner or employe,
whether for hire or not, or play or bet at or against any game of faro, monte,
roulette, lansquenette, rogue et noir, rondo, tan, fan-tan, stud-horse poker,
seven and a half, twenty-one, or any game of chance or banking game, played
with cards, dice, or any device for money, checks, credit, or any other repre-
sentative of value, within the corporate limits of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 2. It shall be unlawful for any person to act as lookout, doorkeeper,
or gamekeeper for any game of faro, monte, roulette, lansquenette, rouge et
noir, rondo, tan, fan-tan, stud-horse poker, seven and a half, twenty-one, or
any other banking or percentage game, or other game of chance played with
cards, dice, or other device, for money, checks, credit, or other representative
of value, within the corporate limits of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 3. It shall be unlawful for any person to visit any room or rooms
within the corporate limits of the City of Los Angeles, where any games of
faro, monte, roulette, lansquenette, rouge et noir, rondo, tan, fan-tan, stud-
horse poker, seven and a half, twenty-one, or any banking game, or game of
chance played with cards, dice, or any device, for money, checks, credit, or
other representative of value is being played, conducted or carried on.

Sec. 4. Itshall be unlawful for any person to keep or exhibit any gambling
table, device or apparatus, or conduct, keep, or carry on any gambling estab-
lishment, or any room or place for the practice of gambling or playing games
of chance for money, or other representative of value, with cards, dice or other
device, within the limits of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 5. It shall be unlawful for any person, either as owner or agent, to
lease or rent any building, room, lot or other place to any person or persons to
be used for gambling, or playing games of chance for money.

Sec. 6. It shall be the duty of the police of said city to seize and safely
keep all chips, checks, cards, boxes, tables, boards and all other articles used
or pertaining to the games of faro, monte, roulette, lansquenette, rouge et noir,
rondo, tan, fan-tan, stud-horse poker, seven and a half, twenty-one, or any
banking game played with cards, dice, or any other device, for money, checks,
credit, or other representative of value, and to produce the same in Court, and
to be retained until the final disposition of any case in which said articles may

===== PDF PAGE 115 =====
 

‘

Title Insurance and Trust Company

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 109

be required as evidence, to be then destroyed by the order of the Judge of the
City Court; but nothing herein contained shall prevent the destruction of said
articles at any time when the Judge of said Court may deem said articles no
longer required to be retained for evidence.

Sec. 7. Any person or persons who shall violate the provisions of this
ordinance shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction
thereof, shall be punished by fine of not more than five hundred dollars, or by
imprisonment for not more than six months, or by both such fine and imprison-
ment.

Sec. 8. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HeERaxpD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

of the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of September 1, 1885.

ORDINANCE No. 194.

An Orprnance to provide for the licensing of business carried on in the City
of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to conduct or
carry on, within the corporate limits of the City of Los Angeles, any vocation,
trade, calling or employment in this ordinance specified, either in their own
names, and for their own profits and benefit, or as agents for any other person
or persons, or body corporate or otherwise, without first procuring from said
city a license so to‘do; and if such person or persons, either for themselves or
as agents, shall conduct or carry on any vocation, trade, calling, business or
employment aforesaid, without having procured such license, he, she or they,
for each violation of this ordinance, shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor,
and upon conviction by any Court having jurisdiction thereof, shall be fined
therefor in a sum not less than ten dollars nor more than two hundred dollars,
or shall be imprisoned for a term not exceeding ninety days, or both, and
the amount of said license shall be deemed a debt due to the said City of
Los Angeles, and all such persons, bodies corporate and their agents, or either

-. of them, shall for each and every violation of this ordinance be liable to an
action in the name of the City of Los Angeles in any Court of competent juris-
diction for the amount of the license of such business as he or they may be
engaged in, with costs of suit.

Sec. 2. That the monthly rates of license for the pursuits, business, trades,
occupations, avocations and employments hereinafter named be and the same
are hereby established for and within the City of Los Angeles, and the same
shall be paid by the owners or proprietors thereof, as follows; that is to say :

For the business of banker, $20.

For every money broker, $5.

For every butcher shop or stall whose monthly sales exceed $400, $3.

For every butcher shop or stall whose monthly sales are under $400, $2.

For every person who, having no butcher shop or stall, engages in the busi-
ness of selling meat inside the city limits, $3; provided, however, that this
shall not apply to occasional sale of meat by persons not engaged in the sale of
the same as a business.

For every undertaker, $5.

For every Cheap John stand, $15.

For every prize picture lottery, $25.

For all persons or corporations not municipal, vending water for domestic
purposes, where the monthly sales do not exceed five hundred dollars, $5 ;
where the monthly sales exceed five hundred dollars and do not exceed one
thousand dollars, $15; for all exceeding one thousand dollars, $25.
