ORDINANCE No. 197. '

An ORDINANCE regulating the registry of dogs, and providing for the taking up
and impounding of dogs without tags.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Itis hereby declared to be unlawful for any person owning or
having charge, care or control of any dog or slut to permit or allow the same to run
at large upon any street, alley, lot, or other public place within the corporate limits
of the City of Los Angeles, unless there shall be attached to such dog or slut a
collar, on which there shall be a tag with an appropriate number, to be obtained
from the City Tax Collector, as hereinafter provided; and it is hereby declared
unlawful for any person to imitate or counterfeit said tag or plate, or use an
imitation or counterfeit of said tag or. plate on any dog or slut within the limits
of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 2. The City Tax Collector shall keep a register, wherein shall be

===== PDF PAGE 125 =====
 

ieee ditle Insurance and Trust Lom pany

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 119

entered the name of the owner of the dog to which a tag has been issued, and
the number and date thereof. The City Tax Collector is hereby directed to
procure the necessary tags mentioned in section (1) one of this ordinance, or
those now in use by the present Poundkeeper, and to annually collect or receive
from the owner of any male dog the sum of two dollars, and from the owner of
any female dog the sum of four dollars for such tag, said tags to have stamped
thereon ‘‘August 14,” (the year to be inserted), and to be good for one year
from date thereof, and he is hereby required to procure, prior to the 14th day of
August in each succeeding year, new tags, with the proper date stamped thereon.
The City Tax Collector shall pay all moneys received for tags into the City
Treasury, according to law, and such monies shall constitute a special fund, to
be known as the Dog Fund; provided, that all dog tags already issued for the
current year shall be good until the expiration thereof.

Sec. 3. The Poundkeeper may appoint such assistants as he may deem
necessary, but all such appointments must be of persons over the age of (21)
twenty-one years; and it is hereby made the duty of the Poundkeeper or his
assistants to take up and impound all dogs found in the streets, alleys, lots, or
other public places within the corporate limits of the City of Los Angeles,
without a tag, as provided for in this ordinance, and to keep such dogs confined
at the public pond (properly provided with food and water) for not less than
five days, unless such dog or dogs be redeemed by the payment of the sum of
two dollars, pound fee, together with the production of the required tag; a
written notice, containing a description of the dogs impounded, shall be posted
up in front of the public pound and in the offic@of the Chief Police, for at least
five days; after the expiration of the above mentioned time, all dogs which
have not been redeemed shall be taken by the Poundkeeper or his assistants
outside of the city limits and killed, and buried not less than one foot below the
surface of the ground, for which service he will be entitled to be paid, out of
the ‘Dog Fund,” the sum of one dollar for each dog killed and buried; pro-
vided, that the Poundkeeper may dispose of any unredeemed dog by gift or sale
to any person who will pay the Poundkeep’s fees,'and procure the necessary
tag for the current year.

Sec. 4. The Poundkeeper shall preserve the ears (and so much of the
scalp as will join them together) of each dog killed and buried, and on the first
Monday of each month deliver the same to the Superintendent of Streets, at
his office, to be counted and destroyed by him; and the said Superintendent of
Streets shall issue to said Poundkeeper a certificate, stating the number of
scalps so counted, which shall be presented to the Council by said Poundkeeper
in his monthly report, and if found to be correct, a warrant shall be ordered
drawn on the ‘‘ Dog Fund” for the amount. But nothing in this ordinance

' shall be so construed as to authorize the issuance of a warrant for the killing

and burying of unredeemed dogs in the pond at the date of the passage of this
ordinance.

===== PDF PAGE 126 =====
120 ORDINANCES AND RESOLTTIONS

Sec. 5. If any person shall interfere with, oppose or resist the Pound-

keeper, or any of his assistants, or any person acting under his direction, while

engaged in performing any duty imposed or authorized by this ordinance, he or
she shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine of not less than ten dollars
nor more than two hundred dollars, or be imprisoned in the city jail not less
than ten days nor more than three months; and if the Poundkeeper or any of
his assistants shall violate any of the: provisiens of this ordinance, such person

shall, upon conyiction thereof, be punished by a fine of not less than ten dollars

nor more than twenty-five dollars, or by both such fine and imprisoment.

Sec. 6. It is hereby made the duty of the Chief of Police, and all police
officers, to arrest all persons violating section one of this ordinance, and to
assist the Poundkeeper and his assistants whenever necessary in the lawful per-
formance of any act required by this ordinance.

Src. 7. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

Src. 8. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heratp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of September 22, 1885.

W. W. ROBINSON,

ORDINANCE No. 198.

Aw Orprnance providing for the punishment of disorderly persons and the
‘keepers of disorderly houses.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person to lie or sleep on any of

===== PDF PAGE 127 =====
 

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 21

the sidewalks, streets, alleys, or other public places within the corporate limits
of the City of Los Angeles, or to appear therein in-sudia state of intoxication
or drunkenness as to be unable to take proper care of himself, or to disturb
the peace or quiet of any person, family or neighborhood by drunkenness, or
by making loud or unusual noises or by violent or offensive language, or by °
boisterous, tumultuous or offensive Conduct, or by threatening, traducing, quar-
reling, fighting or offering or challenging to fight, or in any other way or manner

hood. ~

premises connected with his house, or to be guilty of any riotous or disorderly

ORDINANCE No. 202.

Aw OrprINance regulating riding and driving upon the public streets of the
City of Los Angeles.

===== PDF PAGE 132 =====
126 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS
»
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows.

section 1. The Chief of Police may designate a sufficient number of
police officers to attend on public streets of the City of Los Angeles and control
the movement and order the stoppage of vehicles and animals on said
streets in order that pedestrians, who may be passing or repassing or crossing
said streets, may pass or cross the same with safety.

Sec. 2. Any police officer selected and directed by the Chief of Police to
perform such duty as aforesaid, may control the movement and order the stop-
page of vehicles and animals on such public streets to the end that pedestrians

may pass or cross said streets with safety.

Sec. 3. It shall be the duty of every person driving, using or having the
control of any vehicle or animal upon the public streets of said city to obey the
order of any such designated police officer in regard to moving or stopping any
such vehicle or animal on such public streets.

Sec. 4. It shall be unlawful for any person to immoderately ride or drive
any horse upon any public street of the City of Los Angeles, or to permit any
horse or horses attached to any vehicle to gallop, run or race upon any public
street of said city.

Sec. 5. It shall be unlawful f r any person to ride or drive any horse at
any rate of speed, faster than a walk over or upon any street crossing upon
Main street, between the Plaza and Second street, or upon Spring street north
of Second street.

Src. 6. Any person violating any of the provisions of this ordinance, or
who shall neglect or refuse to obey any order given by a police officer in regard
to the moving or stopping of any animal or vehicle shall be deemed guilty of a
misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not more than fifty
dollars, or be imprisoned not more than fifty days, or suffer both such fine
and imprisonment. >

Sec. 7. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heratp, a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter
it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of November 24, 1885.
W. W. ROBINSON.
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.
Approved this 30th day of November, 1885.

ORDINANCE No. 203.

An Orprmance to regulate the trimming of trees within the City of Los
Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows :

section 1. Every owner, occupant or person having the control or care of
any lot or premises in the City of Los Angeles shall be required to trim any
tree, bush or hedge upon said premises, or upon the sidewalk in front of said
premises, the branches of which interfere with or obstruct persons or vehicles
passing along any public street or sidewalk; all limbs or branches cut off must
be removed from the street without delay.

Sec. 2. Whenever any trees, bushes or hedges are in a condition to inter-
fere with or obstruct persons passing along any public street, the Police Com-
mission shall direct the Street Superintendent to notify the owner or person
having care or control of the. premises upon or in front of which said trees,
bush or hedge, grow, to trim the same within five days after service of notice.

Sec. 3. Any person violating the provisions of this ordinance, or failing
to trim their trees, as aforesaid, within five days after service of notice, shall be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined
not more than fifty dollars, or suffer not more than fifty days imprisonment, i
or suffer both such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HERALD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of December 1, 1885.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 7th day of December, 1885.

E. F. SPENCE,
Mayor.
Published December 8, 1885.

ORDINANCE No. 205.

An Orprvance to establish a paid Fire Department in the City of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. There shall be a Board of Fire Commissioners of the City of
Los Angeles consisting of three (3) persons, citizens of the United States, resi-
dents of the City of Los Angefes for at least two years previous to their ap-
pointment or election as such Commissioner, said Board of Fire Commissioners
to be composed of the Mayor of the City of Los Angeles, President ex-officio,
the President of the Council of said city, and one member of the Council
elected by the Council of said city, who shall hold office until the election and
qualification of their successors; provided that each Commissisner shall serve
until the qualification of a successor, although his term of Councilman may.

===== PDF PAGE 137 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 131

have expired, the Commissioner elected by the Council to hold office for one
year, and to be elected at its meeting for organization each successive year.
The said Commissioners shall, within ten days after their eleetion, meet in the
City Council room, take the usual official oath and file the same with the Clerk
of the Council, and organize by the election of a secretary, who shall receive a
salary of thirty-five ($35) dollars per month. Said Commissioners shall
receive no compensation for their services. Said Commissioners, upon their
organization, shall have power to and are hereby directed and authorized to
make all necessary arrangements, and do and perform all acts necessary to pre-
pare and manage the Fire Department constituted by this ordinance. Said
Commissioners shall, every six months after their organization, make and
submit to the Council estimates for necessary supplies for the Fire Department,
and also shall in the month of July of each year present to the Council esti-
mates of the cost of the Department forthe ensuing year. Said Commissioners
to be supplied with necessary stationery, the cost of which and the salary of
the Secretary shall be paid out of the general fund of the Fire Department,
and said Comiissioners are hereby given full power over the Fire Department
constituted by this ordinance and shall adopt a seal therefor. The Secretary of the
Commission shall, on the first Monday of each month, transmit to the Council
a complete statement of the expenditures of the Fire Department for the pre-
ceeding month. The Fire Department of the City of Los Angeles constituted
by this ordinance shall, when organized, consist of one (1) Chief Engineer, to
be ex-officio Fire Marshal, two (2) steamer companies, one (1) hose company,
one (1) hook and ladder company. The department to be named The Los
Angeles Fire Department and classed as follows: Permanent force—Steamer
Company No. 1, Steamer Company No. 2, Hose Company No. 1 (Park Hose),
Hook and Ladder Company No.1 to be paid companies; East Los Angeles
Hose Company No. 2, Morris Vineyard Hose Company No. 3 to remain volun-
teer companies. Each paid company to be uniformed and equipped with the
necessary hose and apparatus as directed by the Board of Fire Commissioners.

Sec. 2. All officers and members of the Fire Department constituted by
this ordinance shall be appointed by the Board of Fire Commissioners, and
shall be removable at the pleasure of said Board, except the Chief Engineer,
who shall be appointed by the Council and be other than,a member of the
Council. The Chief Engineer appointed under this ordinance shall hold office
for two (2) years. The Chief Engineer appointed under the provisions of this
ordinance may be removed from office by the said Board of Fire Commissioners
for inefficiency, misconduct or misfeasance in office, upon written charges, due
investigation and a fair trial. The Board of Fire Commissioners shall, from
time to time, as they deem necessary, prescribe rules and regulations for the
government of the Fire Department constituted by this ordinance, which shall
be binding thereon and shall be printed and distributed to each member gratis.

All officers and members of the Fire Department shall be at least twenty-one
years of age.

===== PDF PAGE 138 =====
132 ORDINANCES AND RESOLTTIONS

Sec. 3. The Chief Engineer shall receive a salary of one hundred and
twenty-five ($125) dollars per month; each engineer of each engine company
shall receive a salary of one hundred ($100) dollars per month ; each steamer
driver shall receive a salary of seventy ($70) dollars per month; each hose
driver shall receive a salary of seventy ($70) dollars per month ; each hook and
ladder driver shall receive a salary of seventy ($70) dollars per month; each
hook and ladder tilleman shall receive sixty ($60) per month. Each engineer
and driver shall give his whole time to the department, and shall not engage _
in.any other trade, business, or profession or occupation. Each salary to be
due on the last day of each calendar month, and to be paid out of the Fire De-
partment Fund. Said Board of Fire Commissioners shall have no power to
raise the salary of any person connected with the department; they shall have
power to increase or diminish the force.

Sec. 4. The Chief Engineer shall act as Fire Marshal, and attend to all
the duties thereto of such office. He shall give his whole time to the Fire
Department, and shall not engage in any other trade, business, or profession
or occupation. East Los Angeles Hose Company, No. 2, Morris Vineyard Hose
Company, No. 3, will continue a Volunteer Department, subject to all the rules
and regulations of the Board of Fire Commissioners.

Sec. 5. In addition to the permanent force of the Fire Department, there
shall be constituted a call force, as hereinafter specified and classed, and who
shall receive a salary per annum according to rank: Two (2) Assistant Chiefs,
four (4) Foremen, four (4) Assistant Foremen, thirteen (13) hosemen, two (2)
firemen, five (5) hook and ladder men; total, twenty-four (24) men. One (1)
Foreman, one (1) Assistant Foreman, and four (4) hosemen be apportioned for
each steamer company. Hose Company No. 1, apportioned one (1) Foreman,
one (1) Assistant Foreman and four hosemen. Hook and ladder Company No.
1, apportioned one (1) Foreman and Assistant Foreman, and four (4) hook and
ladder men. Each call Foreman to receive a salary of one hundred and eighty
($180) dollars per annum; each call hoseman to receive a salary of hundred
and forty-four ($144) dollars per annum; each call hook and ladder man to
receive a salary of one hundred and forty-four ($144) dollars per annum.

Sec. 6. Atits first regular meeting, after the taking effect of this ordinance,
the Council of the City of Los Angeles shall appoint one of its members to
serve as Fire Commissioner, until the appointment and qualification of his
successor, and thereupon the Commissioners shall proceed to qualify and
organize in accordance with the provisions of this ordinance.

Sec. 7. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict herewith are
hereby repealed.

Sec. 8. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herap, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

ORDINANCE No. 207A.

AN OrpINANCE to provide for the better protection of the City of Los Angeles
from the spreading of contagious diseases.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be the duty of each and every physician in the City of
Los Angeles to report in writing to the Health Officer of said city the name and
residence of every patient he shall have, within the limits of said city, affected
with scarlet fever, smallpox or other contagious disease. Such physicians shall
also ascertain and report in writing to the Health Officer the names of all chil-
dren belonging to the same family or household as his patient so affected with
any contagious disease, who attend the public schools of said city, together with
the name and location of the school so attended. He shall also instruct the
parent or person having the control of such children not to permit them to
attend school until the Health Officer shall pronounce all danger of contagion

past.

===== PDF PAGE 141 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 135

Sec. 2. The Health Officer upon receiving any such report of children
attending public schools, shall immediately transmit the names to the princi-
pals of schools attended, if known, and if unknown to the City Superintendent
of Schools.

Sec. 3. It shall be unlawful for any parent or person having the care or
control of any child to permit such child to attend any school in the City of Los
Angeles while any member of the same family or household, as said child is
affected with scarlet fever, smallpox or other contagious diseases, or before the
Health Officer shall pronounce all danger of contagion removed.

Sec. 4. Any person who shall fail to comply with, or who shall violate any
of the provisions of this ordinance, shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor,
and, upon conviction, shall be fined not more than two hundred dollars, or be

imprisoned not more than six months, or suffer both such fine and imprison-
ment.

sec. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of December 22, 1885.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 26th day of December, 1885.

E. F. SPENCE,
Mayor.
Published December 27, 1885.

ORDINANCE No. 209.
Aw OrprNance prohibiting the selling of adulterated milk.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person to offer or have for sale in
the City of Los Angeles any unwholesome, watered or adulterated milk, or
milk known as swill milk, or milk from cows that are fed on swill, garbage or
any like substance, nor any butter or cheese made from any such milk.

Sec. 2. The Health Officer shall inspect milk sold in the city at such times
as he may deem proper, and in addition thereto, shall whenever complaint is

made to him that any person is selling adulterated milk shall inspect the milk
sold by such person.

===== PDF PAGE 144 =====
138 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 3. Whenever the Health Officer shall find any milk inspected by
him to be adulterated, impure or unwholesome, he shall cause the same to be
thrown out and. destroyed.

Sec. 4. Any person violating the provisions of this ordinance, or who
shall refuse to permit the Health Officer to inspect and test his milk, or who
shall refuse to destroy the same when directed so to do by the Health Officer,
shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall
be fined not more. than two hundred dollars, or suffer imprisonment for not
more than six months, or suffer both such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of January 19, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

thereon—that is to say, commencing at a point east of the Plaza, and thence
running southerly on and along Los Angeles and Carlisle streets, over each side
of the center line thereof to the southern boundary of the city; also a branch

thereof, to Pearl street; also a branch commencing at.the intersection of Los

Provided, that no turnout or switch shall be constructed, except in places

ORDINANCE No. 211.

Aw Orprnance providing for blockading the streets and alleys, and the preser-
vation of Fire Department property during fires.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Whenever a fire shall break out in the City of Los Angeles it
shall be lawful for the Chief Engineer, or Acting Chief Engineer, of the Fire
Department of the City of Los Angeles to blockade any street, alley, lane, court
and place, or such part thereof as in his judgment may be necessary to insure
the efficient working of the men and engines under his command, and to pro-
tect the hose of the department from injury by passing vehicles and street cars,
and it shall be the duty of the Chief of Police to furnish a sufficient detail of
policemen during any such fire to protect the lines of blockade from being
broken through, or the hose or other Fire Department property from being in-
jured ; and the said Chief of Police shall render the Chief Engineer, or whoever

~

===== PDF PAGE 148 =====
142 ORDINANCES AND RESOLTTIONS

may be acting in that capacity, all the assistance in his power in carrying out
the provisions of this ordinance.

Sec. 2. All steam engines and other moving apparatus of the Fire De-
partment of the City of Los Angeles shall have paramount right of way through
all streets, lanes, alleys, courts and other places in the City of Los Angeles
when running to a fire, and such apparatus together with all other vehicles
belonging thereto, shall take and keep the right side of the street, unless the
same be obstructed, and all street cars in the vicinity of any such apparatus
going to a fire shall retard or accelerate their speed, as occasion may require, in
order to give the apparatus of the department the unobstructed use of the street
for the time being.

Sec. 3. Any person or persons breaking through or attempting to break
through the blockade mentioned in section (1) one of this ordinance, or running
over with any vehicle or street car the line of hose in use at a fire, or any per-
son or persons having the control of any vehicle or street car who wilfully or
carelessly permits the same to obstruct the progress of the apparatus of the
Fire Department going to a fire, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon
conviction thereof, be punished by a fine of not less than five dollars nor more
than fifty dollars, or by imprisonment of not less than five or more than fifty
days, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 4. Any person or persons wilfully injuring any engine house, engine,
hose, hose carriage, or other apparatus of the Fire Department of this city shall
be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction, shall be fined
not less than fifty dollars, or be imprisoned in the city jail not less than fifty
days nor more than six months, or shall be punished by both such fine and im-
prisonment.

Sec. 5. All ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

Sec. 6. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
annce, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of January 26, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 2d day of February, 1886.

E. F. SPENCE,
Mayor.

ORDINANCE No. 213.* :

Aw OrprNance granting a franchise for the construction and operation of a
street failroad in the City of Los Angeles to the Main street and Agricul-
tural Park Railroad Company, a corporation.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the right of way be and the same is hereby granted to the
Main Street and Agricultural Park Railroad Company, a corporation, and to its
successors, over and along the public streets of said city named in; this ordi-
nance, for the period of thirty years from and after the passage of this ordinance,
for the purpose of making all necessary excavations for and constructing, laying
down, maintaining and operating a street railroad, with necessary turnouts and
switches, with iron or steel rails; Provided, that no rails known as T rails shall
be used in the construction ‘of this road, and running cars thereon to be drawn
and propelled by horses, with the right at any time within the life of this fran-
chise to adopt and substitute an electric, cable, thats to say.:

Commencing at the present terminus of the Main Street and Agricultural
Park Railroad on Main street, near the foot of Temple street, and running
thence southerly along Main street to a point twenty-five feet south of the
southerly line of First street, from which point there shall be double tracks along
Main street to its intersection with Washington street, equi distance from, and
upon each side of the center of Main street, with five feet space between the
tracks; thence westerly along Washington street to Figueroa street; thence
southerly along Figueroa street to Jefferson street; thence westerly along Jeff-
erson street to Wesley avenue; thence southerly along Wesley avenue to the
city limits, also connecting with said road as above described at the intersec-
tion of Main and Washington streets, and running thence southerly along the
center of Main street to Jefferson street; thence westerly along the center of
Jefferson street to Figueroa street, at which point it shall connect with the
track now laid and operated by said company, adopting and incorporating as a
part and parcel of this franchise the track now owned, occupied and operated
by said Main Street and Agricultural Park Railroad Company upon and over
the streets heretofore mentioned, as well also as that laid and used by said
company from the intersection of Main and Washington streets, easterly along
Washington street to its stables on the corner of Washington and Carlisle
streets, excepting therefrom, however, that portion now laid and operated on
Main street, commencing twenty-five feet south of the southerly line of First

street and thence to Washington street, which portion shall be taken up and
removed.

Provided, and upon condition, that the said grantee, or its successors, shall
plank, pave or macadamize the entire length of said route along which said

===== PDF PAGE 151 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 145

road may be constructed, between the rails, and for two feet on each side thereof,
and shall keep the same constantly in repair, flush with the grade of the streets,
and provided with good crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all neces-
sary and proper flumes and culverts for the free and uninterrupted passage of
water under said tracks from lands higher than said tracks or roadbed is
required to be, and that there be sufficient space between the tracks and each
of the tracks and side tracks or turnouts to allow the cars to pass each other
freely and without danger.

And provided, further, that the laying of said tracks, except as hereinafter
provided, shall conform in all cases when any grade has been established, to
such established grade, and in all other cases to the natural grade of the streets
through which they may run, and when at any time any part of the said route
shall be graded, or the grade thereof changed or altered, the bed of the road
and the tracks thereof shall be made to conform therewith.

Provided, further, that when the streets along said route, or any of them
are paved or macadamized, or after having been paved or macadamized, shall
at any time be repayed or macadamized with other material or in a different
manner the said grantee or its successors shall repave or macadamize it, said
route, between the rails, and for two feet on each side thereof, with the like
material and in the same manner to correspond with said street.

Provided that the rate of fare for any distance along said road shall at no
time exceed five cents for one passenger, and the owners of said road shall pay
to the City of Los Angeles such license for each car as may be required by the
ordinance of said city.

Sec. 2. It is understood that the grant of this franchise gives to the grantee
or its successor the right, whenever they may deem it necessary or expedient,
to lay down and maintain a double track upon any or all portions of the route

hereinbefore described, excepting that portion extending from First street north-
erly along Main street.

It is further understood, that the city, in making the grant of this fran-
chise, expressly reserves the right to grade, renew, sewer, pave, macadamize,
improve, alter or repair all or either of said streets, or any part thereof, and to
lay down pipes for water, gas and other purposes ; such work to be done by the
city, so as to obstruct or injure said road as little as possible.

Src. 3. Provided, that no turnout or switch shall be constructed except in
places designated by the Council of the City of Los Angeles, nor shall such
turnout in any case be nearer than twenty-five feet to the junction of any two
streets, or the intersection of any cross-streets, The City Surveyor shall desig-
nate the radii of course to be used in swinging the lines of this road from one

street to another, where it is necessary to change the direction, and of sidings
and switches,

===== PDF PAGE 152 =====
146 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 4. The above rights and privileges are granted upon the express con-
dition that the said road shall be commenced within three months, and fully
completed, equipped, stocked and in running order within one year from and
after the passage of this ordinance. Any failure to complete said road within
the time above designated, shall operate as a forfeiture of the right of way on
such portion of the line as may remain uncompleted at such date.

It is further understood, that the franchise is especially granted upon all
and each of the provisos and conditions herein contained, and if said grantee
or his assigns shall fail in any particular to comply therewith, or with either of
them, then and in that case all rights to this franchise, except as hereinbefore
stated, shall be thereby forfeited, and this grant shall be null and void, and that
nothing herein contained shall be construed in any manner as granting an ex-
clusive franchise.

Sec. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herap, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

_ I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council
of the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of February 9, 1886.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.
Approved this 18th day of February, 1886.

EK. F. SPENCE,

ORDINANCE No. 215.

Aw OrDINANCE establishing water rates and fixing the compensation for water

===== PDF PAGE 155 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 149

to be furnished by any person, company or corporation for family uses, for
private purposes, and for other uses in the City of Los Angeles for the year
commencing July 1, A. D. 1886. , :

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. The monthly rates of compensation to be collected by any
person, company or corporation engaged in the business of supplying water
to’ the inhabitants of the City of Los Angeles for domestic and other pur-
poses, for the year commencing July 1, A. D. 1886, and ending June 30,-A. D.
1887, are hereby fixed as follows:

, For tenements occupied by a single family, including bathtub and water
closet, one dollar and fifty cents ($1.50).

Horses kept for private use, including water for washing one vehicle, fifteen
(15) cents; each additional horse, ten (10) cents; each additional vehicle, ten
(10) cents.

For hose for washing windows, sidewalks, garden or grounds, not including
lawns, for every lot not more than sixty (60) feet front, twenty-five (25) cents;
over sixty (60) feet front and not exceeding one hundred (100) feet front, fifty
(50) cents; over one hundred (100) feet front, one (1) cent per front foot for all
over one hundred (100) feet, in addition to the rate for one hundred (100) feet.

For hose for washing windows, sidewalks, gardens or grounds, including
lawns, for every lot not more than sixty feet front, fifty (50) cents; over sixty
feet front and not more than one hundred (100) feet, seventy-five (75) cents;
over one hundred (100) feet front, two (2) cents per foot for all over one hundred
(100) feet, in addition to the rate for the one hundred feet.

For each water closet used in public buildings, one dollar and fifty ($1.50)
cents.

For each urinal used in public buildings, seventy-five (75) cents.

For water used for building purposes, for each barrel of lime used, ten (10)
cents.

For bakeries, for each barrel of flour used, three (3) cents.

Stores, banks, offices, warehouses, saloons, groceries, barber shops,
butcher shops, blacksmith shops, book binderies, confectioners, churches, halls,
laundries, photograph galleries, printing offices, steam engines, green houses,
markets, market stores, soda fountains, and other places of business not sup-
plied by meter, to be charged according to the estimated quantity used, from
one (1) to ten (10) dollars; when meters are used, then if the quantity used
does not exceed ten thousand gallons per month, for each one thousand gallons,
twenty-five (25) cents; over ten thousand gallons per month, at the rate of
fifteen (15) cents for each one thousand ( 1,000) gallons.

===== PDF PAGE 156 =====
150 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Hotels, boarding houses, boarding schools and lodging houses, in addition
to family rate, ten (10) cents for each boarder or lodger.

For every bathtub used in barber shop, bathing establishment or hotel,
two (2) dollars. f

For each horse trough on public streets, fifty (50) cents.

Fountains outside of city parks shall be regulated by contract.

All persons, companies or corporations, furnishing water as aforesaid, shall
have the right in all cases to apply meters, at their own expense, for the pur-
pose of discovering waste or excessive use, and when waste or excessive use is
found to charge meter rates. ;

For water supplied for purposes not specified in the above tariff the rate,
shall be in proportion to the above tariff when meters are n t used, and the
meter rates where meters are used.

All water furnished for sprinkling streets, flushing sewers, watering
parks, or for the extinguishing fires, shall be supplied free; provided, that
when the City of Los Angeles is not entitled by law or contract to water free for
the extinguishing fires or sprinkling streets, the rate on each hydrant used for
extinguishing fires shall be twenty (20) cents per month; and on each hydrant
used for sprinkling streets, one ($1) per month.

No company or person furnishing water shall charge more than the actual
cost of labor and materials for inserting tap and putting in service pipe.

All rates, except meter rates, are due and payable in advance, and meter
rates are due and payable at the end of the month, and upon meter rates a
deposit not exceeding three-fourths (34) of the value of the estimated quantity
of water to be consumed for the month may be required.

Sec. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heravp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of February 26, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

approval March 22, 1886. By reason of not being returned within fifteen days

effective and as valid as if the Mayor had approved and signed it.

ORDINANCE No. 216.

Aw Orprvance regulating the issue of fishing permits, and of permits to parties
having pipes connected with the zanja.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the Zanjero or Water Overseer shall, upon the 25th day
of each month, get from the Mayor a certain number of fishing permits to be
printed for one day, with date left blank; also, a certain number of monthly
permits to parties having water pipes connected with the zanjas, and permits to
other parties paying for privileges upon the zanjas; each of such permits shall
be good only for the time mentioned on its face, and shall be signed by the
Mayor and Water Overseer, and shall be sold only for cash.

The Water Overseer shall, at the expiration of each week, make a full and
satisfactory settlement with the Mayor for said permits, by reporting the amount
paid to the City Treasurer, exhibiting the Treasurer’s receipt therefor, and the
Mayor shall keep an account thereof, with the account for other water permits,
wherein shall be entered the number of permits issued to Water Overseer, and
the amount of said permits in cash; and if any are returned unsold at the end
of the month, then the same shall be entered in said book to the credit of the
Water Overseer, and the Mayor shall, at the first meeting in each month of the
Council, report the number, kind and cash value of all permits delivered to the
Water Overseer for the previous month, ending on the 25th day thereof, and
the amount of cash reported to him by the said Water Overseer as having been
paid to the City Treasurerer, and shall further report to and deliver to the City
Council all the unused permits returned by the Water Overseer for cancellation.

Sec. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HERALD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of March 23, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.
Approved this 2d day of April, 1886.

. F. SPENCE,
Mayor.

ORDINANCE No. 219.

An OrpinaNnce to amend an ordidance, entitled ‘‘An Ordinance granting a
franchise for the construction and operation of a street railroad in the City
of Los Angeles to the Main Street and Agricultural Park Railroad Com-
pany, a corporation,” approved on the 18th day of February, 1886, and
being numbered 213.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1, That part of section (1) one of an ordinance, entitled ‘An
Ordinance granting a franchise for the construction and operation of a street
railroad in the City of Los Angeles to the Main street and Agricultural Park
Railroad Company, a corporation,’ approved the 18th day of February, 1886,
and being numbered 213, from the beginning of said section to and including
the word ‘‘cable” immediately preceeding the words ‘‘that is to say’’ before the
description of the route designated, is hereby amended by striking out the
words ‘“‘provided that no rails known as T rails shall be used in the construction
of this road,’’ and inserting instead thereof the words ‘‘said rails to be pro-
vided with plank on the outside of each rail not less than four inches wide, to

_ be spiked to the cross ties and up to and flush with the top of the rail along the
entire route and to be kept in good repair,’”’ and also by inserting between the
words ‘‘electric’”’ and ‘‘cable”’ the word ‘‘or,’’ and by inserting after the word
“cable” the word ‘‘system,’’ so that said part of said section 1, as amended,
shall read as follows:

Section 1. That the right of way be and thesameis hereby granted to the
Main Street and Agricultural Park Railroad Company, a corporation, and to its
successors, over and along the public streets of said city named in this ordi-
nance, for the period of thirty years from and after the passage of this ordinance,
for the purpose of making all necessary excavations for and constructing, laying
down, maintaining and operating a street railroad, with necessary turnouts and
switches, with iron or steel rails, said rails to be provided with plank on the

===== PDF PAGE 162 =====
156 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

outside of each rail, not less than four inches wide, to be spiked to the cross
ties, and up to and flush with the top of the rail along the entire route, and to
be kept in good repair, and running cars thereon to be drawn and propelled by
horses, with the right at any time within the life of this franchise to adopt and
substitute an electric or cable system.

ORDINANCE No. 221.
An Orpryance regulating the building of bridges across the Los Angeles river.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. No bridge shall be erected or built over or across the Los
Angeles river which shall be less than three hundred feet in length, or with
spans of less than one hundred feet in length. Provided, that before any
bridge shall be built over or across the Los Angeles river the plans thereof
shall be submitted to and approved by the City Surveyor and Board of Public
Works of the Council of the City of Los Angeles,

Src. 2. Any person, firm or corporation which shall fail to comply with
the provisions of this ordinance, shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and
each days continuance of a structure erected in violation of this ordinance shall
be deemed a separate offense, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished
by a fine of not more than five hundred dollars, or by imprisonment for not
more than six months, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily

HERALD, a newspaper published in said city, and thereupon and thereafter it
shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of March 16, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

The foregoing ordinance was presented to the Mayor for his approval
March 22, A. D, 1886, and returned by him to the Clerk of the Council, without
_his approval, on April 14, A. D. 1886. By reason of not being returned
within fifteen days (Sundays and other legal holidays excepted) the above

ordinance has become effective and as valid as if the Mayor had approved and
signed it.

ORDINANCE No. 224.

An Orprxnace to regulate houses of ill-fame and prostitution, and to prohibit
them in certain places in the City of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. No person shall keep, maintain or carry on any bawdy house, ~
or place of ill-fame or prostitution any where in the City of Los Angeles outside
of the following limits:

Commencing at the center of High street and New High street, and run-
ning thence southerly along New High street to the center of Temple street ;
thence westerly along the center of Temple street, to the center of Fort street ;
thence southerly along the center of Fort street, to the center of Third street;
thence easterly along the center of Third street, to the center of Main street;
thence southerly along the center of Main street, to the center of Mayo street ;
thence easterly along the center of Mayo street, to the center of Los Angeles
street ; thence northerly along the center of Los Angeles street, to the center of
First street; thence along the center of First street easterly to a point 200 feet
east of the east line of Alameda street; thence northerly parallel with Alameda
street, to its intersection with a prolongation of center line of High street. Nor
shall any bawdy house, or place of ill-fame or prostitution be kept, maintained

or carried on in any one-story house, nor in the basement or on the ground
floor of any building within said limits,

===== PDF PAGE 166 =====
160 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 2. No person shall live or stay temporarily in any place for the pur-
pose of carrying on, or assisting in carrying on, the business of fornication
for hire in any house or place where, by the first section of this ordinance, a
bawdy house, or place of ill-fame or prostitution is forbidden to be kept, main-
tained or carried on.

Sec. 3. No person shall enter into any bawdy house, or place of ill-fame
or prostitution for the purpose of patronizing the same, or its inmates in such
business, which house or place is kept, carried on or maintained contrary to the
provisions of this ordinance.

Sec. 4. The keeping a bawdy house, place of ill-fame or prostitution, con-
trary to the first section of this ordinance is a nuisance, and the violation of any
provision hereof is a misdemeanor, and punishable by fine not exceeding two
hundred dollars, or by imprisonment not exceeding sixty days, or by both such
fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 5. All ordinances and resolutions, and parts of ordinances and reso-
lutions in conflict with this ordinance are hereby repealed.

Sec. 6. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HeERALp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of March 30, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

approval, April 23, A. D. 1886. By reason of not being returned within fifteen

ORDINANCE No. 231:

An OrpINANCE of the City of Los Angeles relating to the regulations, sale and
disposition of the water and zanjas of the city for irrigating purposes.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. The following is the price of water for irrigating inside of the
city limits, to-wit:

For one day, two (2) dollars per head.

For one-half day, one dollar and twenty-five cents ($1.25) per head.

For one night, one dollar and twenty-five cents ($1.25) per head.

For one hour, fifty (50) cents per head.

One day shall be regarded from sunrise to sunset. The hour water shall
be sold at the discretion of the Zanjero.

Sec. 2. If at any time there shall be a surplus of water unsold at the
times specified in the ordinances of said city providing for the time of applying
for water for irrigating purposes, the Zanjero may grant the use of the several
zanjas of said city for the purpose of carrying water through the same to per-
sons residing outside of the limits of said city for the following prices, to-wit:

For the use of any zanja or part thereof carrying one head of water, for one
day, four (4) dollars.

For one night, two (2) dollars,
For the use of any zanja carrying two heads, for one day, eight (8) dollars.
For one night, four (4) dollars.

Nothing herein contained shall be construed as a relinquishment on the

part of the city to fully control the disposition of the use of the water of Los
Angeles river for irrigating purposes.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heratp, and that it shall take effect on the 26th day of May, A. D. 1886.

ORDINANCE No. 236.

An Orpinance forbidding all persons from connecting private sewers with other
private sewers which are connected with the public sewers.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person to connect a private sewer
from his property with a private sewer on any other property which is connected
with the public sewers, without permission of the proper authorities of the City
of Los Angeles.

Src. 2. Any person or persons who shall violate the provisions of this
ordinance shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction
thereof, shall be punished by a fine of not more than one hundred dollars, or by
imprisonment for not more than one hundred days, or by both such fine and

imprisonment.

Src. 38. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of June 28, 1886.

ORDINANCE No. 237.

AN ORDINANCE requiring the grip-slot on cable roads to be maintained at a width
of not more than three-quarters of inch.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. All persons, companies or corporations owning or operating
cable railroads in the limits of the City of Los Angeles shall maintain the grip-
slot on said roads at a width of not more than three-quarters of an inch, except
on curyes, where it shall be not more than one inch wide.

Sec. 2. Any person, persons or corporations who shall violate the pro-
visions of this ordinance, shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon
conviction thereof, shall be punished by a fine of not more than one hundred
dollars, or by imprisonment for not more than one hundred days, or by both
such fine and imprisonment. And every day during which any violation of
this ordinance continues, shall be considered as constituting a new offense, and
be punishable as in this section provided.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herap, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council
of the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of June 28, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 6th day of July, 1886.

E. F. SPENCE
Mayor.

Published July 7, 1886.

ORDINANCE No. 244.

An ORDINANCE regulating the use of the Public streets of the City of Los
Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person to use the public sidewalks
for the display of merchandise or to leave any goods, merchandise, boxes, bar-
rels, trucks or other articles upon any portions of the public streets of the City
of Los Angeles, described as follows:

Main street, from Plaza to Third street; Spring street from Temple to
Third street; First street, from Fort street to Los Angeles; Second street, from
Fort street to Main street; Requena street, from Main street to Los Angeles
street; Arcadia street, fom Main street to Los Angeles street ; Commercial
street, from Main street to Alameda street.

Src. 2. All merchandise placed upon the public sidewalks of the portions
of the streets described in section (1) one of this ordinance shall be immedi-
ately taken into the stores or removed by the owner thereof.

Src. 8. It shall be unlawful for any person to use any of the sidewalks or
gutters of the portions of the streets described in section (1) one of this ordi-
nance for the purpose of packing or unpacking goods or merchandise.

===== PDF PAGE 187 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 181

Src. 4. It shall be unlawful for any person, between the hours of 7 o'clock
A.M. and 6:30 o’clock p. ., to leave any horse standing hitched for a longer period
than one hour on any of the portions of the streets described in section (1) one
of this ordinance, or to leave any express wagon, truck, hack, herdic, delivery
or other wagon backed up against the curb of any portion of the public streets
described in section (1) one of this ordinance, except when the same is being
actually used for the delivery or receiving of goods and passengers.

Sec. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HERALD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of

ORDINANCE No. 250.
AN ORDINANCE regulating the operation of street railroads.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. All persons, companies or corporations owning or operating
street railways in the City of Los Angeles are hereby required, within thirty
(30) days after the taking effect of this ordinance, to place upon all street cars
running and used upon said roads, numbers in plain and conspicuous figures,
running consecutively from one (1) upward, on each side and each end of each
car used on said road.

Sec. 2. No person or corporation owning or operating a street railway shall
permit more than forty persons to be carried at one time upon any car drawn
by one horse, or more than sixty persons upon any car drawn by two horses.

Sec. 38. Any person or corporations who shall violate, neglect or refuse
to comply with the provisions of this ordinance, shall be deemed guilty of a
misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by a fine of not
more than one hundred dollars, or by imprisonment of not more than one
hundred days, or by both such fine and imprisonment. And every day during
which any violation of this ordinance continues, shall be considered as consti-
tuting a new offense, and shall be punished as in this section provided.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council
of the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of August 30, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 6th day of September, 1886.

E. F. SPENCE,
Mayor.

ORDINANCE No. 253.*

An Orprinance regulating the use of the Public streets of the City of Los
Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows :

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person to use the public sidewalks
for the display of merchandise or to leave any goods, merchandise, boxes, bar-
rels, trucks or other articles upon any portions of the public streets of the City
of Los Angeles, described as follows:

Los Angeles street, from Arcadia street and Aliso street to First street;
Main street, from the Plaza to Third street; Upper Main street, from Marches-
sault street to junction of Upper Main street and Alameda street; Spring street,
from Temple street to Seventh street; First street, from Fort street to Los
Angeles street; Second street, from Fort street to Main street; Requena street,
from Main street to Wilmington street; Arcadia street, from Main street to
Los Angeles street; Commercial street, from Main street to Alameda street.

Sec. 2. All merchandise placed upon the public sidewalks of the portions
of the streets described in section (1) one of this ordinance shall be immedi-
ately taken into the stores or removed by the owner thereof.

Sec. 3. It shall be unlawful for any person to use any of the sidewalks or
gutters of the portions of the streets described in section (1) one of this ordi-
nance for the purpose of packing or unpacking goods or merchandise.

Sec. 4. It shall be unlawful for any person, between the hours of 7 o’clock ~
A.M. and 6:30 o’clock p. m., to leave any horse standing hitched for a longer period
than one hour on any of the portions of the streets described in section (1) one
of this ordinance, or to leave any express wagon, truck, hack, herdic, delivery
or other wagon backed up against the curb of any portion of the public streets
described in section (1) one of this ordinance, except when the same is being
actually used for the delivery or receiving of goods and | assengers.

Sec. 5. Any person who shall violate any of the provisions of this ordi-
nance shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof,
shall be fined not more than two hundred ($200) dollars, or be imprisonmed

===== PDF PAGE 197 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 19]

in the City Jail not more than six (6) months, or suffer both such fine and im-
prisonment.

Sec. 6. Allordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

Sec. 7. The Clerk of the Council shall certify tot e passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HERALD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of September 13, 1886.
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.
Approved this 21st day of September, 1886.
E. F. SPENCE,
Mayor.

ORDINANCE No. 254.

An Orprvance granting a franchise to the Central Street Railway Company to
extend its track along Chestnut and Hoff streets, in the City of Los
Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the right of way be and the same is hereby granted to
the Central Street Railway Company, and to its assigns, over and along the
public streets of said city named in this ordinance, for the period of thirty
years from and after December 6, 1877, for the purpose of extending its present
track and constructing, laying down, maintaining and operating a street rail-
road track with iron or steel rails, and to run cars thereon, to be drawn or pro-
pelled by horses or mules, and to carry passengers thereon ; the rails to be used
in the construction of said road shall be provided with plank on the outside of
each rail not less than four inches wide and flush with the top of the rail along
the entire route, and to be kept in good repair; that is to say:

Commencing at the center of its present track on Downey avenue, near
the crossing of said Downey avenue with Chestnut street; running thence

===== PDF PAGE 198 =====
192 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

along Chestnut street to Hoff street; thence along Hoff street northeasterly to
Daly street, with the right to construct such turnouts and switches as may be
necessary to operate said road successfully, said track to connect with and
form a part of the present street railroad of said company, and the whole line
to be operated as one and the same line, and only one fare to be collected for
travel over the whole line from each passenger. It being understood and
agreed that throughout the entire description the center of each street, or a line
as near thereto as practicable, is intended.

Provided, and upon condition, that the said grantee or its assigns shall
plank, pave or macadamize the entire length of said route along which said
road may be constructed, between the rails, and for two feet on each side
thereof, to correspond with said streets when the same shall be paved or
macadamized, and shall keep the same constantly in repair, flush with the
grade of the streets, and provided with good crossings for all kinds of vehicles,
and with all necessary and proper flumes and culverts for the free and uninter-_
rupted passage of water under said track from lands higher than said' track or
roadbed; and that the track be not more than five feet wide within the rails;
and there be a space between the main tracks and side tracks or turnouts, if
any side track there be, sufficient to allow cars to pass each other freely and
without danger.

Provided, further, that the laying of said track, except as hereinafter stated,
shall conform in all eases, when the grade of any of said streets has been
established through which said track may run, to such established grade, and
in all other cases to the natural grade of said street, and when at any time any
part of the route shall be graded or the grade thereof changed, or altered, by
. said Council, the bed of the road, and the tracks thereof, shall be made to
conform therewith.

Provided, further, and upon condition that if at ‘any time for the space of
six months the said road or any portion thereof be unused as a street railroad
the franchise for the said portion so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

Provided, further, that the rate of fare for any distance along said road
shall not be greater than that heretofore authorized to be charged by said com-
pany, and only one fare shall be charged for travel over the whole connected
line of said company for each passenger; and the owner or owners of said road
shall pay to the City of Los Angeles the same license for each car as heretofore
required of said company by the ordinance of said city.

Sec. 2. It is understood that the city, in making the grant of this fran- —
chise, expressly reserves the right to grade, renew, sewer, pave, macadamize,
improve alter or repair all or either of said streets or any part thereof, and to
lay down pipes for water, gas and other purposes; such work to be done by the
city so as to obstruct or injure such road as little as possible, but when such ~

===== PDF PAGE 199 =====
; OF THE CITY. OF LOS ANGELES. 193

work makes the same necessary the owner or owners of said road must shiff
the rails so as to avoid the obstruction made thereby.

Sec. 3. The above rights and privileges are granted upon the express con-
dition that the said road shall be commenced within one month and fully com-
pleted, equipped, stocked and in running order from the point of commence-
ment at Chestnut street to the termination thereof on Daly street, within four
months from the date of taking effect of this ordinance. It being understood,
and agreed, that this franchise shall be forfeited by the grantees herein on
account of a failure to complete the said road, or parts thereof, as above pro-
vided, within the periods respectively hereinbefore set forth, only for such
portion or portions of said road, which at such date or dates, respectively, shall
remain and be unfinished, leaving the franchise to that portion of the road
completed and in running order, unaffected by such failure.

Sec. 4. The City Surveyor shall designate the radii of curves to be used
in swinging the lines of this road from one street to another, where it is
necessary to change the direction, and of sidings and switches, and shall give
the established grade, when called upon so to do, of the streets along the line
of said proposed track, and on the construction of said road shall set grade
stakes along said line, indicating the grade of said streets, so that the track
may be placed in accordance therewith; the R. R. Co. to pay expense of City
Surveyor for same.

Sec. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

‘L hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of September 20, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 25th day of September, 1886.

that there be a space between the main track and side tracks or turnouts suf-
ficient to allow the cars to pass each other freely and without danger.

And provided, further, that the laying of said tracks shall conform, in all
cases where any grade has been established, to such established grade, and in
all other cases, to the natural grade of the streets through which they may be
constructed; and when at any time any part of said route shall be graded, or
the grade thereof changed or altered, the bed of the road and the tracks thereof
shall be made to conform therewith.

Provided, further, and upon condition that at no time shall the fare for any
distance along said road exceed the sum of five cents for one fare.

Provided, further, and upon condition that if at any time, for the space of
six months, the said road, or any portion thereof, be unused as a street railroad,
the franchise for the said portion so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

Sec. 2. It is understood that the city expressly reserves the right to grade,
sewer, pave, macadamize, improve, alter or repair all or either of said streets,
or any part thereof, throughout the whole length of said road, and to lay down
pipes for water, gas or other purposes; such work to be done by the city, so as
to obstruct or injure the said road as little as possible, but when work makes
the same necessary, the owner or owners of said road must shift the rails, so as
to avoid the obstruction made thereby.

It is further understood, that this franchise is especially granted upon each
and all of the provisions and conditions herein contained and reserved, and if
said grantee, or its successors or assigns, shall fail in any particular to comply
therewith, or with either of them, then and in that case all rights to this fran-
chise shall be thereby forfeited, and this grant shall be null and void, and that
nothing herein contained shall be construed as granting an exclusive franchise.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Hera.p, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of September 20, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,

ORDINANCE No. 256. ;
An OrpbINANCE relating to the fire-alarm telegraph.
The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows :

Section 1. No person shall break, remove or injure any of the parts or
appurtenances of the fire-alarm telegraph without authority or permission of
the Board of Fire Commissioners. No person shall make or fit any key, to the
lock of any signal box of the fire-alarm telegraph without authority of the
Chief Engineer of the Fire Department. No person shall have or retain in his
possession, or under his control, a key belonging to or fitted to open the lock of
any such signal box, without lawful authority of the Fire Commissioners or
Chief Engineer of the Fire Department or Superintendent of the fire-alarm
system. No person shall wilfully make or cause to be made any false alarm
of fire by means of said telegraph or otherwise, (and a reward of twenty-five
dollars will be paid by the Council of the City of Los Angeles for the arrest and
conviction of any person for giving, by means of the fire-alarm telegraph, a
false alarm of fire.)

Sec. 2. No person shall put or place, maintain or suffer to be or remain,
any article thing or matter, on or upon the sidewalk so as to obstruct or inter-
fere with the free access or approach to any signal box of the fire-alarm tele-
graph.

Sec. 3. Any person moving or intending to move any house, structure or
building likely to interfere with said fire-alarm telegraph, shall at once give
notice to the Chief Engineer or’ Superintendent of the fire-alarm system, and
shall at once make provisions for the immediate repair of any injury or of any
disturbances of said fire-alarm telegraph, and, provided, that no interference
for said cause shall take place between the hours of 5 o’clock in the evening and
8 o’clock in the morning.

Sec. 4. No person or corporation shall run any wire on any of the telegraph
poles or fixtures of the fire-alarm telegraph of the City of Los Angeles, or run,
erect, or maintain any wire crossing, or running parallel to, any wire of said
fire-alarm telegraph within a distance of six feet.. No person shall, with intent
to deceive, falsely represent himgelf to be an employe of the fire-alarm telegraph
of said city. No person owning or controlling property along the lines of said
fire-alarm telegraph shall allow any branch or limb of any tree, shrub, or vine
to be within six feet of said fire-alarm telegraph.

Sec. 5. Any person violating any of the provisions of this ordinance shall
be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be
punished by a fine not exceeding five hundred dollars, or be imprisoned in the
city jail not exceeding ten days, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

ORDINANCE No. 263.

An Orprnance to provide for the suppressing and prohibiting the keeping of
places for the smoking of opium.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to keep a room,

===== PDF PAGE 212 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 205

building, arbor, booth, shed or tenement to be used or occupied for the purpose
of eating, smoking or inhaling of opium within the corporate limits of the City
of Los Angeles; or if, as the owner, su erintendent or agent of any room, build-
ing, arbor, booth, shed or tenement, or other premeses, he shall become aware
that the same is used or occupied for the purpose of eating, smoking or inhaling
opium, and shall fail, within a reasonable time after having obtained such
knowledge to report the same to the Chief of Police of the City of Los Angeles,
he shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on conviction, be pun-
ished by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars or more than two hundred
dollars, or be imprisoned in the city jail not exceeding two hundred days, or by
both such fine and imprisonment.

Src. 2. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to visit any room,
arbor, shed, booth or tenement within the corporate limits of the City of Los
Angeles where the smoking, eating or inhaling of opium is being carried on,
under a penalty, on conviction, of a fine not exceeding one hundred dollars, or
imprisonment in the city jail not exceeding ninety days, or both.

Sec. 3. It shall be unlawful for any person or persons to act as lookout or
doorkeeper, or tender, or to exhibit any box, pipe, cup, thing or appartus, at
any place where the eating, smoking or inhaling of opium is being carried on,
under a penalty, on conviction, of a fine not exceeding two hundred dollars, or
imprisonment not exceeding ninety days, or both.

bec. 4. It shall be the duty of the police of said city to sieze and safely
keep all cups, pipes, apparatus, boxes and things used for the purpose of eating,
inhaling or smoking of opium, and produce the same in Court, and to be re-
tained until the final disposition of any case in which said articles may be
required as evidence, to be then destroyed by order of the Court, but nothing
herein contained shall prevent the destruction of said articles at any time when

the Judge of “said Court may deem said articles no longer required to be
retained for evidence.

Sec. 5. All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

Sec. 6. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to t-e passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
HERALD, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of November 15, 1886.
'
W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 4. The said grantee shall within six months from and after the date
of the taking effect of this ordinance, complete the laying down, building and

said. That if at any time for the space of ninety days said road or any part
thereof shall be unused as a railroad, the franchise for said road or the part
thereof so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

Sec. 5. In the construction of said railroad along the line of any of said
streets within said city, the said grantee shall place the rails of said road in
such way that the top of the rail shall be flush with the street, and the laying
of the track shall conform in all cases where any part of said route has been
graded, according to such established grade, and in all other cases as near as
practicable to the natural grade and surface of the street; and whenever at any
time any part of said streets shall be graded, or the grade thereof changed or
altered, by the Council of said city, then the bed of the road and the tracks
thereof shall be changed and shifted by the said grantee so as to conform to such
new official grade; and whenever the said road shall cross any zanja or water
ditch, used for irrigation within said city, good and proper culverts shall be
constructed so as not to interfere with or impede in the slightest degree the
flow of water therein; and whenever at any time the said route shall intersect
any street now or hereafter to be opened across any of the said streets along

street forming a junction with any of said streets, along which said right-of-way
is hereby granted, then and in such case the said grantee shall construct and

and in a like manner to correspond with said streets, and shall keep the same
constantly in repair, flush with the streets, and provided with good crossings for
all kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary and proper flumes and culverts for
the free and uninterrupted passage of water from rains or other drainage; and it
shall be further required to keep safe and secure all street crossings and places
where said railroad crosses any canal, zanja or ditch, at its own expense.

Provided, further, and upon condition that at no time shall the rate of fare
for any distance along said road within the city limits exceed the sum of five
cents for one fare; and provided, further, that the fare for any child under the
age of eighteen years, while going to and from any public school, shall be one-
half the regular fare, and said company shall pay the license required by ordi-
nance of said city.

and conditions herein named and contained, and if at any time the said grantee,

its successor or assigns, shall fail or neglect to comply therewith in any respect

ORDINANCE No. 267.
Lease of water to Citizen’s Water Company.

AN ORDINANCE,

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows :

Section 1. The Mayor of the city is authorized and directed to execute,
in the name of the city, to the Citizen’s Water Company, a lease of the same
tenor and effect, and in the same form as the draft of lease annexed hereto.

Provided, that the price of water supplied by said company shall not be
greater than that charged by the City Water Company for similar service; and

Provided, that this lease shall in no wise affect the right of the Council of
the City of Los Angeles to impose a license and regulate water rates.

Sec. 2. This ordinance shall be in force from and after its passage, ap-
proyal and publication. ‘ :

DRAFT OF LEASE.

 

This Indenture, made this day of November, 1886, between the City
of Los Angeles, a municipal corporation, party of the first part, and the Citi-
zen’s Water Company, a corporation, the party of the second part,

Witnesseth, that the said party of the first part, for and in consideration of the
contracts and agreements on the part of the party of the#econd part herein con-
tained, have leased and let, and hereby do lease and let unto the party of the
second part, that certain part of the waters of the City of Los Angeles diverted at
or above the tunnel constructed on the Lick tract by Wicks and Mills from the
main supply ditch, and at one other point, such as approved by the City Council
of the City of Los Angeles, or its successors in office, for the use of the resi-
dents of the City of Los Angeles; said amount of water to be equal, whether
diverted at one or two places, to twenty inches of water, miners’ measurement,
under six-inch pressure.

In consideration of said lease, the said party of the second part agrees,
during the continuance of said lease, to carry through the pipes of the said
party party of the second part, free of charge or expense to said city, such
water as the city may take for the necessary use within the district supplied
with water by said second party for all city buildings, public parks, public
squares, public fire hydrants, public schools, flushing of sewers and public
sprinkling hydrants, established at the expense of the city in said district; but
it is understood and agreed, that said water so run for the benefit of and free |
of expense to the said City of Los Angeles, shall not be estimated as any part
of the said twenty inches, but the same is an addition thereto.
