to pay ten per cent. of the whole amount of expense of maintaining any acqueduct
belonging to the city from which said company diverts any portion of the water
aboye mentioned, from the point of such diversion to the source of the water
supply. In case of hereafter cementing the main ditch or piping said water,

new inyestment from point of diversion to source of supply.

This contract shall not extend beyond July 22, 1898, but may be severed
by either party by resolution of the Board of Directors of party of the second

ORDINANCE No. 268.

' An Orpinance providing for the construction and repairing of Sidewalks on
certain streets in the City of Los Angeles.

‘

 

===== PDF PAGE 222 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 215

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. Whenever any portion of any street, lane or alley, court or
place in the City of Los Angeles, improved, or any sidewalk constructed thereon
according to law shall be out of repair and in condition to endanger persons or
property passing thereon, or in condition to interfere with the public conven-
ience in the use thereof, it shall be the duty of the Superintendent of streets to
require, by notice in writing to be delivered to them personally, or left on the
premises, the owners or occupants of lots, or portions of lots, fronting on said
portion of said street, lane, alley, court or place, or of said portion of said walk
so out of repair, as aforesaid, to repair forthwith said portion of said street,
lane, alley, court or place to the center thereof, or said sidewalk in front of the
property of which he, the owner, tenant or occupant, and said Superintendent of
Streets shall specify in said notice what repairs are required to be made. After
the expiration of three days from the date of the service of said notice, the said
Superintendent of Streets shall be deemed to have acquired jurisdiction to con-
tract for the making of repairs required by said notice. If said repair shall not
be commenced within three days after notice given, as aforesaid, and diligently
and without interruption prosecuted to completion, the said Superintendent of
Streets may, under authority from the City Council of the City of Los Angeles, .
make such repair or enter into a contract with any suitable person, at the
expense of the owner, tenant or occupant, at a reasonable price, to be deter-
mined by said Superintendent of Streets, and such owner, tenant and occupant
shall be liable to pay the same. Upon the completion of said repairs by said
contractor, as aforesaid, to the satisfaction of the Superintendent of Streets,
said Superintendent of Streets shall make and deliver to such contractor a cer-
tificate to the effect that said repairs have been properly made by said con-
tractor, and that the charges for the same are reasonable and just, and that he,
said Superintendent, has accepted the same.

Sec. 2. ‘That hereafter, all sidewalks, and the repair of all sidewalks of
such portion of the following named streets of said city, as are hereinafter de-
scribed, shall be made and constructed of flat, smooth, even stone, either
natural or artificial, or asphaltum, and not otherwise than as above stated.
The streets and portions of streets are:

Main street,on both sides thereof, from Marchessault street to the north
line of Twelfth street.

On both sides of Spring street, from the south line of Temple street to the
north line of Ninth street.

On both sides of Fort street, from Temple street to Tenth street.
On both sides of Los Angeles street, from Arcadia street to First street.

On the east side of San Fernando street, from Railroad street to Downey
avenue.

_ mentioned in section two of this ordinance, shall be constructed and repaired

be removed before such filling.

failing, neglecting or refusing to repair or construct sidewalks, after due notice
given, within the time and in the manner specified in the notice therefor, as
hereinbefore provided, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction
thereof, shall be fined not more than fifty dollars, or be imprisoned not more
than fifty days, or suffer both such fine and imprisonment, and every additional
day during which any person shall fail to repair or construct sidewalks, after
due notice therefor, as hereinafter provided, shall constitute an additional
offense, and shall be punishable as hereinbefore specified.

ORDINANCE No. 269.

An Orprvance to prevent the soliciting of prostitution in the City of Los
Angeles. :

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful for any woman to offer her body for the
purpose of prostitution, or solicit any man for money to have carnal intercourse

with her, or to commit fornication with, within the corporate limits of the City -
of Los Angeles.

Sec. 2. Any person violating the provisions of this ordinance, shall be
deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on conviction be punished by a
fine not exceeding one hundred dollars, or by imprisonment not exceeding one
hundred days, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Hera.p, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of November 22, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.
Approved this 2d day of December, 1886.
E. F. SPENCE,

Mayor.
Published December 6, 1886.

An OrpINANCE granting a franchise for the construction and operation of a

Geo. C. Knox, and their assigns.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the right of way be and the same is hereby granted to
J. M. Thompson and Geo. C. Knox, and their assigns, over and along the

===== PDF PAGE 229 =====
y ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

~

bo

public streets of the city named in this ordinance, for the period of thirty
years from and after the date of the passage of this ordinance, for the purpose
of making the necessary excavations for and constructing or laying down,
maintaining and operating a double-track cable street railroad, with iron or
steel rails, and running cars thereon, propelled by cable; that is to say:

Commencing at the intersection of New High street with the northern
boundary of Franklin street, and running thence northerly along New High
street, on each side of the center line thereof, to Virgin street; thence westerly
along Virgin street, on each side of the center line thereof, to Buena Vista
street; thence northeasterly along Buena Vista street, on each side of the center
line thereof, to Hoff street; thence northeasterly along Hoff street, on each

westerly boundary of Chestnut street.

Provided and upon condition that said grantees, or their successors or
assigns, shall plank, pave or macadamize the whole of said road, between the
rails and for two feet on each side thereof, up to and flush with the top of the
rail, and shall keep the same constantly in repair, flush with the grade of the
street, and provided with good crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all
necessary and proper flumes for the free passage of water under said track,
whenever and wherever the Council of said city, or the successors; shall order
said repairs, or other work above specified to be done; and that there be suf-
ficient space between the tracks and side tracks or turnouts to allow the cars of
said road to pass each other freely and without danger; and that the width of
said track shall not be greater than three and one-half feet between the rails;
and that the roadbed and track shall conform, in all cases where a grade has
been established, to such grade, and in all other cases, to the natural grade of
the streets through which they may run, and when at any time the whole
or any part of said route shall be either graded, paved or otherwise improved,
or the grade or improvement thereof changed or altered, the bed of the road,
and the track thereof shall be, by the grantee or assigns, made to conform, in
grade or material, or both, therewith.

And provided, further, that no turnouts or switches shall be constructed in
places other than those designated by said City Council, or its successors, which
authority also shall prescribe the radii of curves to be used in swinging the line
of said road from one street to another.

And provided, further, that at no time shall the fare for any distance along
said road exceed the sum of five cents for one passenger; and persons who shall
attend the public schools of said city, as pupils, shall be required to pay but
one-half of said fare on any of its cars, to or from said schools; provided, said
pupils shall purchase their fare in quantities of at one dollar’s worth at one time ;
and said grantees or assigns shall provide for and sell such fares to said pupils,
or for their benefit, at all times when solicited so to do.

And provided, that the grantee or assigns of said road shall, on or before
the 15th day of December of each year, pay to said city such license upon each
car as may be required by the ordinances of said city.

And proyided, further, that if at any time for the space of three months
the said road or any portion thereof shall be unused as a street railroad, the
franchise for the portion so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

Src. 2. Itis expressly understood and agreed, that the city expressly re-
serves the right to use and control the streets herein named and in any way
affected by this ordinance, for any and all purposes, the same as if no such
franchise existed ; such use to be made so as to injure or obstruct said road as

that throughout the entire route granted said road, the center of the street, or
a line as near thereto as practicable, is intended.

grantees or their assigns the right to excavate for and construct, lay down and

And it is further understood that the grant of this right carries with it the

full running order and operation within one year from the taking effect of this
ordinance; and any failure to complete said road within the time above pre-
scribed, shall operate as a forfeiture of the right of way over any portion of the
same then uncompleted.

Furthermore, this franchise is especially granted upon each and all of the

fail in any particular to comply therewith, then and in that case, all rights
’ under this ordinance, shall thereupon and immediately be forfeited, and this
grant shall thereupon be null and void; and nothing herein contained shall be
construed as granting an exclusive franchise.

nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Trisung, and there-
upon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

approved by the City Surveyor of said City of Los Angeles, and are now on file

property owners adjacent to said river, pursuant to a former resolution of the
City Council, shall be commenced as soon thereafter as said material shall
arrive at said city. The work of the construction of said levee shall be prose-
cuted without any unnecessary delay, as rapidly as the material therefor can
reasonably be obtained, and shall be continued without interruption, except by
unavoidable accident, until the levee shall be completed.

After its completion, the levee shall thereafter be kept and maintained in

good order and condition by said railway company, its successors or assigns,
without expense to said city.

of way are hereby granted, then, and in such case, the said railway company,
its successors or assigns, shall construct and maintain good, proper and sub-
stantial board crossing the whole distance across or in front thereof.

Src. 12. The city reserves the right to grade, renew, sewer, pave, macad-
amize, improve, alter or repair any or all parts of said streets, over which said
rights of way are hereby granted, and to lay down pipe therein for water, gas
and other purposes, and to construct sewers and zanjas over and along the
same, but such work is to be done by the city so as to injure said road as little
as possible, and the’city shall have the right at any and all times to use, manage
and control the said streets as public streets to the same extent and with the
same power, whenever deemed necessary, as if this right-of-way had not been
granted.

Src. 13. Whenever said city shall desire to extend or prolong any of the
public streets of said city across the lands hereby granted to said railway com-
pany and across the official bed of said Los Angeles river to such parts of said
city as lie eastwardly of said river, it shall have the right (such right being
hereby reserved) as public convenience may require, and to extend, prolong
and improve such streets through and across any portion of said land over and
across the tracks to be laid by said railway company upon said land (provided
the same can be done without disturbing or injuring any buildings or other
improvements that may be erected on said lands by said railway company, its
successors or assigns, for railroad purposes); and also to construct bridges over
said river upon the line of said streets, and proper approaches thereto; and to
construct and pass under said railway tracks along the line of said streets, any
water canals or zanja, gas pipe or water ditch, at the expense of said city; in
such case said railway company, its successors or assigns, shall correspond its

===== PDF PAGE 238 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 2a.

railway tracks to the required grade of such streets, water canal, zanja or ditch,
the expense of changing the said track or tracks in such case, to conform to the
said grade of said canals and streets, to be at the expense of said railway
company, its successors or assigns.

Sec. 14, Said railway company, its successors or assigns, shall pave, plank
or macadamize the entire length of said railway tracks across said streets, be-
tween the rails and for two feet on each side thereof; and at any time when any
of the streets in the city across which said railway tracks shall run, shall be
paved, repaired or macadamized with other material, and in a different manner,
then the said railway company, its successors or assigns, shall pave, repave or
macadamize between the rails and two feet on each side thereof, with the same
material and in a like manner, to correspond with said streets, and shall keep
the same constantly in repair, flush with the streets, and provided with good
crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary and proper flumes and
culverts for the free and uninterrupted passage of water from rains or other
drainage, and it shall be further required to keep safe and secure all street
crossings and places where said railway tracks shall cross any canal, ditch or
zanja, at its own expense.

Src. 15. Ths right-of-way hereby granted over said streets is given upon
each and all of the terms and conditions herein named and contained, and-if
at any time the said railway cémpany, its successors or assigns, shall fail or
neglect to comply therewith, in any respect or particular, then, and in that
event all such rights of way shall thereupon become forfeited to said city.

Sec. 16. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance and shall cause the same to be published at least once a week for eight

consecutive weeks in the Trimune, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take
effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council
of the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of December 8, 1886.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the right of way be and the same is hereby granted to

===== PDF PAGE 241 =====
254 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

H. J. Crow, and assigns, over and along the public streets of said city
hereinafter named, for the period of thirty years from and after the taking
effect of this ordinance, for the purpose of making all necessary excavations,
constructing, laying down, maintaining and operating a single (or double) track
railroad, with iron or steel rails, and necessary turn-outs, or switches, the cars
thereof to be drawn or propelled by steam, viz. :

Commencing at the intersection of Hayes and Hoff streets, and running
thence along Hayes to Arroyo street, thence along center of Arroyo street to
Well street, thence along Well street to Columbus street, thence along Colum-
bus street to Cypress avenue, thence along Cypress avenue to the north bound-
ary of the City of Los Angeles.

Proyided and on condition that said grantee, or his successors or
assigns, shall plank, pave or macadamize the whole of said road between the
rails and for two feet on each side thereof, and provide it for its entire length
with wooden stringers, not less than four inches wide, spiked to the ties against
the outside of and up to and flush with the top of the rail, and shall keep the
same constantly in repair, flush with the grade of the street and provided with
good crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary and proper
flumes for the free passage of water under said track, and that there be sufficient
space between the tracks and sidetracks, or turnouts, to allow the cars of said
road to pass each other freely and without danger; and that the width of said
track shall not be greater than 4’ 814” feet between the rails ; and provided further,
that the roadbed and track shall conform, in all cases where a grade has
been eStablished, to such grade, and in all other cases, to the natural grade of
the street through which they run, and when at any time the whole or
any part of said route shall be either graded, paved or otherwise improved,
or the grade or improvement thereof changed or altered, the bed of the road,
and the tracks thereof shall be, by the said grantee or assignee, if so required by
said City Council or its successors, made to conform, in grade or material, or
both, therewith.

And provided, further, that no turnouts or switches shall be constructed in
places other than those designated by said City Council, or its successors, which
authority also shall prescribe the radii of curves to be used in swinging the line
of said road from one street to another.

And provided, further, that at no time shall the fare for any distance along
said road exceed the sum of five cents for one passenger; and that persons who
attend the public schools of said city, as pupils, shall be required to pay but
one-half of said fare on any of its cars, from or to said schools; provided, said
pupils shall purchase their fare in quantities of at least one dollar’s worth at a
time; and said grantees or assigns shall provide for and sell such fares to said
pupils, or for their benefit, at all times when solicited so to do.

And proyided, further, that the grantee or assigns of said road shall, on

===== PDF PAGE 242 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES, 239

or before the 15th day of December of each year, pay to said city such license
fee upon each car as may be required by the ordinances of said city.

And provided, further, that if at any time for the space of three months
the said road or any portion thereof shall be unused as a railroad, the franchise
for the portion so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

Sec. 2. It is understood and agreed, that the city expressly reserves the
right to use and control all its public streets for any and all purposes, the same
as if no such franchise existed; such use to be made so as to obstruct or injure
said road as little as possible, and when work upon or other use of said streets
makes the same necessary, the grantee or assigns of said road shall shift the
same at its own expense, so as to ayoid the obstruction made thereby. It is
understood that, throughout the entire route granted said road, the center of
the street, or a line as near thereto as practicable, is intended.

Sec. 3. The above rights and privileges are granted upon the express con-
dition that the said road shall be commenced and completely equipped and in
full running order and operation'within twelve months from the date of the
taking effect of this ordinance; and any failure to complete said road within
the time above prescribed, shall operate as a forfeiture of the right of way over
any portion of the same then uncompleted.

Furthermore, this franchise is especially granted upon each and all of the
provisions and conditions herein contained, and if said grantees or assigns shall
fail in any particular to comply therewith, then and in that case, all rights
under this ordinance shall thereupon and immediately be forfeited, and this
grant shall thereupon be null and void; and nothing herein contained shall be
construed as granting an exclusive franchise.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Trreung, and there-

ORDINANCE No. 279.

An Orprvance to prohibit the obstruction of the public streets, crosswalks and
the entrances to public halls and buildings in the City of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

===== PDF PAGE 246 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 239

Section 1. The sidewalks and crosswalks of the city, and the entrances to
public halls and publie buildings within the city limits, being intended for the
accommodation and convenience of the public, shall be kept and reserved free

therein at any time are prohibited.

same so as inany manner to obstruct the free passage thereon, or to hinder
molest or annoy any person in passing along the same, or obstruct or stand
around the entrances of said public halls or public puildings.

Src. 2. Any person who shall violate any of the provisions of this ordi-
nance shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction, shall be
fined not more than fifty dollars, or be imprisonment not more than sixty days!
or suffer both such fine and imprisonment.

nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Trisunr and thereupon

track shall not be greater than that of the Second street cable road ; and provided,
further, that the roadbed and track shall conform (in all cases where a grade has
been established, to such grade) and in all other cases, to the natural grade of
the streets through which they run, and when at any time the whole or
any part of said route shall be either graded, paved or otherwise improved,
or the grade or improvement thereof changed or altered, the bed of the roads,
and the tracks thereof shall be, by the grantee or assignee, made to conform, in
grade or material (or both) therewith.

And provided, further, that no turnouts or switches shall be constructed in
places other than those designated by said City Council, or its successors, whose
authority shall also prescribe the radii of curves to be used in swinging the line
of said road from one street to another.

And provided, further, that at no time shall the fare for any distance along
said road exceed the sum of five cents for one passenger; and that persons who
attend the public schools of said city, as pupils, shall be required to pay but
one-half of said fare on any of its cars, to or from said schools; provided, said
pupils shall purchase their fare in quantities of at least one dollar’s worth at a
time; and said grantees or assigns shall provide for and sell such fares to said
pupils, or for their benefit, at all times when solicited to do so.

And provided, further, that the grantees or assigns of said road shall, on
or before the fifteenth day of December of each year, pay to said city such
license fee upon each car as may be required by the ordinances of said city.

And provided, further, that if at any time, for the space of three months,
the said road, or any portion thereof, shall be unused as a street railroad, the
franchise for the portions so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

Sec. 2. It is understood and agreed, that the city expressly reserves the
right to use and control all its public streets for any and all purposes, the same
as ifno franchise existed. Such use to be made so as to obstruct or injure the said
road as little as possible; and when work upon, or other use of said streets
makes the same necessary, the grantees or assigns of said road shall shift the
same at its own expense, so as to avoid the obstruction made thereby. It is
understood that throughout the entire route granted said road, the center of the
street is intended, so far as the same is now, a public deeded street.

===== PDF PAGE 251 =====
244 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 3. The above rights and privileges are granted upon the express con-
dition that the said road shall be completed and completely equipped and im
full running order and operation within one year from the date of the taking
effect of this ordinance, and any failure to complete said road within the time
above prescribed, shall operate as a forfeiture of the right of way over the

entire route.

Furthermore, this franchise is expressly granted upon each and all of the
provisions and conditions herein contained, and if said grantees or assigns shall
fail in any particular to comply therewith, then and in that case all rights
under this ordinance shall thereupon and immediately be forfeited, and this
grant shall thereupon be null and void, and nothing herein contained shall be
construed as granting an exclusive franchise.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause.the same to be published once in the Trmuns, aud there-
upon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council
of the City’of Los Angeles, at its'meeting of February 1, 1887.

FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 8th day of February, 1887.

ORDINANCE No. 284.

Aw Orprnance establishing water rates and fixing the compensation for water

to be furnished by any person, company or corporation for family uses, for

private purposes and for other uses in the City of Los Angeles for the year
commencing July 1, A. D. 1887.

===== PDF PAGE 253 =====
246 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. The monthly rate of compensation to be collected by any
person, company or corporation engaged in the business of supplying water to
the inhabitants of the City of Los Angeles for domestic and other purposes for
the year commencing July 1, A. D. 1887, and ending June 30, 1888, are hereby
fixed as follows: :

For tenements occupied by a single f mily, including bath tubs and water
closets, one dollar and fifty cents ($1.50) ;

Horses kept for private use, including water for washing one vehicle, fifteen
(15) cents; each additional horse, ten (10) cents; each additional vehicle, ten
(10) cents.

For hose for washing windows, sidewalks, gardens or grounds, not includ-
ing lawns, for every lot not more than sixty (60) feet front, twenty-five (25)
cents; over sixty (60) feet front and not exceeding one hundred (100) feet front,
fifty (50) cents;

Over one hundred (100) feet front, one (1) cent per front foot for all over
one hundred (100) feet in addition to the rate per one hundred (100) feet.

For hose for washing windows, sidewalks, gardens or grounds, including
lawns, for every lot not more than sixty (60) feet front, fifty (50) cents; over
sixty (60) feet front, and not more than one hundred (100) feet, seventy-five
(75) cents; over one hundréd (100) feet front, two (2) cents per front foot for all :
over one hundred (100) feet in addition to the rate for the one hundred (100)
feet.

For each water closet used in public buildings, one dollar and fifty ($1.50)
cents.

For each urinal used in public buildings, seventy-five (75) cents.

For water used for building purposes, for each barrel of lime used, ten (10)
cents.

For bakeries, for each barrel of flour used, three (3) cents.

Stores, banks, offices, warehouses, saloons, groceries, barber shops, butcher
shops, blacksmith shops, book binderies, confectioners, churches, halls, laun-
dries, photograph galleries, printing offices, steam engines, green houses,
markets, market stores, soda fountains and other places of business, not supplied
by meter, to be charged according to the estimated quantities used, from one (1)
to ten (10) dollars.

When meters are used, then, if the amount used does not exceed ten
thousand gallons per month, for each one thousand gallons, twenty-five (25)
cents; over ten thousand gallons per month, at the rate of fifteen (15) cents for
each one thousand gallons.

===== PDF PAGE 254 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 247

Hotels, boarding-houses, boarding-schools and lodging-houses, in addition
to family rates, ten (10) cents for each boarder or lodger.

For every bath tub used in a barber shop, bathing establishment or hotel,
two (2) dollars.

For each horse trough on public street, fifty (50) cents.

Fountains outside of city parks shall be regulated by contract.

All persons, companies or corporations furnishing water, as aforesaid, shall
have the right in all cases to apply meters at their own expense for the pur-

pose of discovering waste or excessive use, and when waste or excessive use is
found to charge meter rates.

The water supplies for purposes not specified in the above tariff the rate
shall be in proportion to the above tariff where meters are not used, and the
meter rates where meters are used.

All water furnished for sprinkling streets, flushing sewers, watering parks,
or for the extinguishing of fires shall be supplied free; provided, that when
the City of Los Angeles is not entitled by law or contract to water free, for the
extinguishing of fires or sprinkling streets, the rate of each hydrant used for
extinguishing fires shall be twenty (20) cents per month, and on each hydrant
used for sprinkling streets one (1) dollar per month.

No company or person furnishing water shall charge more than the actual
cost of labor and materials for inserting tap and putting in service pipe.

All rates, except meter rates, are due and payable in advance, and meter
rates are due and payable at the end of the month, and upon meter rates a
deposit not exceeding three-fourths (34) of the value of the estimated quantity
of water to be consumed for the month may be required.

and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

ORDINANCE No. 285.

Aw Orpinance ordering all persons laying or putting down any sidewalk, gutter,
curb, or grading any street or part thereof, to conform with grades furnished
by the City Surveyor, and fixing penalty for violation thereof.

curb, or any person or persons grading any street, or part thereof, must do the
same in conformity with the grades furnished them by the City Surveyor, and

ordinance shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, upon conviction
thereof, shall be fined not more than fifty dollars, or be imprisoned not more
than fifty days, or both, in the discretion of the Court.

ORDINANCE No. 291.

An ORDINANCE granting to the Central Street Railroad Company a franchise for
the construction of a street railroad in the City of Los Angeles,

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the right of way be and the same is hereby granted to
the Central Street Railroad Company and its assigns, over and along the
public streets of said city hereinafter named, for the period of thirty years
from and after the date of the taking effect of this ordinance, for the purpose
of making all necessary excavations, constructing, laying down, maintaining
and operating a double track street railroad, with iron or steel rails, and neces-
sary turn-outs or switches; the cars thereon to be drawn or propelled by horses
or mules, with the right at any time during the life of this franchise to adpot
and substitute an electric or cable system, viz:

===== PDF PAGE 263 =====
256 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Commencing at the corner of Main and Arcadia streets, and running
thence to Aliso street; thence along Aliso street easterly to Alameda street;
thence along Alameda street southerly to Sansevain street; thence along San-
sevain street to Vignes street; thence along Vignes street southerly to First
street; thence to the depot to be erected on the grounds formerly. owned by
Mrs. Bigelow, on such street as may be opened for that purpose, over such
right of way as may be secured by said company.

Provided and on condition that said grantee, or its successors or
assigns, shall plank, pave or macadamize the whole of said road between the
rails and for two feet on each side thereof, and provide it for its entire length
with wooden stringers, not less than four inches wide, spiked to the ties against
the outside of and up to and flush with the top of the rail, and shall keep the
same constantly in repairs flush with the grade of the street, and provided with
good crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary and proper
flumes for the free passage of water under said track, and that there be suffi-
cient space between the tracks or turnouts to allow the cars of said road to pass
freely and without danger; and that the width of said track shall not be greater
than 314 feet between the rails.

7

And provided, further, that the roadhed and track shall conform in all
cases where a grade has been established, to such grade, and in all other.
cases to the natural grade of the streets through which they run, and when at
any time the whole or any part of said route shall be either graded, paved or
otherwise improved, or the grade or improvement thereof changed or altered,
the hed of the road and the track thereof shall be by the grantee or assigns, if
so required by said City Council or its successors, made to conform in grade and
and material, or both therewith.

And provided, further, that no turnouts or switchs shall be constructed in
places other than those designated by said City Council, or its successors,
which authority shall prescribe the radii of curves to be used in swinging the
line of said road from one street to another.

And provided, further, that at no time shall the fare for any distance along
said road exceed the sum of five cents, and that said road shall be operated in
connection with the other lines of*road of said company, and only one fare
shall be charged for one ride over the whole or any part of their lines of road,
and that persons who attend the public schools of said city as pupils, shall be
required to pay but one-half of said fare, on any ofits cars from or to said schools;
provided, said pupils shall purchase their fare in quantities of at least one dol-
lar’s worth at a time, and said grantee or assigns shall provide for and sell such

' fares to said pupils, or for their benefit at all times, when solicited so to do,

And provided, further, that the grantee or assigns of said road shall on

===== PDF PAGE 264 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 257

or before the 15th day of December of each year, pay to said city such license,
fee upon each car as may be required by the ordinances of said city.

And provided, further, that if at any time for the space of six months
the said road or any portion thereof shall be unused ag a street railroad, the
franchise for the portion so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

It is understood that the Central Railway Company, in accepting this
franchise, agrees to transfer passengers over all lines of their road without any
charge other than the sum designated in this ordinance.

It is further understood that this ordinance grants the right to run over
the Boyle Heights and Aliso Street Railroad Company’s tract on Arcadia, Los
Angeles and Aliso streets, from the corner of Main and Arcadia streets to the
corner of Aliso and Alameda streets, and the further right to lay one line of
track along Los Angeles, Aliso and Alameda streets from the corner of Arcadia
and Los Angeles streets to the corner of Alameda and Sainsevain street, said
track to be and the track of the Boyle Heights and Aliso Street Railroad Com-
pany to be equi-distant from the center of the street, and a double track over
the balance of t e route mentioned in this ordinance.

Src. 2. It is understood and agreed, that the city expressly reserves the
right to use and control all its public streets for any and all purposes, the same
as if no such franchise existed; such use to be made so as to obstruct or injure
said road as little as possible, and when work upon or other use of said streets
makes the same necessary, the grantee or assigns of said road shall shift the
same at its own expense, so as to avoid the obstruction made thereby. It is
understood that, throughout the entire route granted said road, the center. of
the street, or a line as near thereto as practicable, is intended.

Sec. 3. The above rights and privileges are granted upon the express con-
dition that the said road shall be commenced and completely equipped and in
full running order and operation within one year from the date of the
taking effect of this ordinance; and any failure to complete said road within
the time aboye prescribed, shall operate as a forfeiture of the right of way over
the entire route.

Furthermore, tlis franchise is especially granted upon each and all of the
provisions and conditions herein contained, and if said grantee or assigns shall
fail in any particular to comply therewith, then and in that case, all rights
under this ordinance shall thereupon and immediately be forfeited, and this
grant shall thereupon be null and void; and nothing herein contained shall be
construed as granting an exclusive franchise.

ORDINANCE No. 295:

An OrpINANCE regulating the number of hacks, express wagons and other
vehicles and providing a record thereof.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Srection 1. That all hacks, carriages or other vehicles used for the purpose
of carrying passengers to and fro within the corporate limits of the City of Los
Angeles for hire, and all express wagons and other vehicles used for carrying
baggage, merchandise and other goods to and fro within said city for hire shall
be numbered, and said number shall be in plain arabic figures, and at least
three inches in length and of width to correspond,

Src. 2. The numbers above referred to shall be furnished by the Chief of
Police to owners of vehicles at actual cost, and it shall be the duty of every

===== PDF PAGE 269 =====
262 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

person, persons or corporation owning any vehicle as prescribed in settion 1 of
this ordinance to secure such numbers of the Chief of Police and place the
same in a conspicuous place upon their vehicles. Said Chief of Police shall
keep a record of every vehicle thus furnished with numbers, the name of the
owner and the number.

Sec. 3. Any person, persons or corporation who shall violate any provi-
sion of this ordinance after April 1, 1887, shall be deemed guilty of a misde-
meanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not to exceed one hundred
dollars, or in default of the payment thereof, shall be imprisoned not to exceed

thirty days.

Sec. 4. All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict with this ordi-
nance are hereby repealed.

Sec. 5. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Trieune, and thereupon and thereaiter it shall take effect and be in force.

IT hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of March 14, 1887.

Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 19th day of March, 1887.

ORDINANCE No. 308.
AN ORDINANCE in regard to bridges over the Arroyo Seco.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That all bridges hereafter constructed over the Arroyo Seco,
within the corporate limits of the City of Los Angeles, shall be constructed of
at least one span of, one hundred feet in length, and that all private bridges
- across said stream shall be built subject to approval by the proper city author-
ities.

Sec. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Trisune, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of May 2, 1887.

FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of City of Los Angeles.

ORDINANCE No. 310.

Aw Orprnancr granting to Ralph Rogers and ris assigns a franchise for the
construction of a street railroad in the City of Los Angeles.

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. That the right of way be and the same is hereby granted to
Ralph Rogers and assigns, over and along the public streets of said city here-
inafter named, for the period of thirty (30) years from and after the date of
taking effect of this ordinance for the purpose of making all necessary excava-
tions, constructing, laying down, maintaining and operating a single track
street railway, with iron or steel rails, and necessary turnouts or switches; each
car thereof to be drawn or propelled by two horses, two mules, electricity or
wire cable running under the ground, viz:

Commencing at point of intersection of the centerline of Hoff street with the
center line of Chestnut street, and running thence along Hoff street to Daley
street; thence along Daley street to Pasadena ayenue; thence along Pasadena
avenue to the northern boundary of the City of Los Angeles, with a right to
cross the Arroyo Seco upon a bridge to be constructed by said grantee or his
assigns, to be at least one span of 100 feet long, and the bridge to be constructed
by the grantee in the manner approved by the proper city authorities, to be
attached to the side of the bridge constructed across said Arroyo Seco and said

===== PDF PAGE 291 =====
284 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

s

Daley street by said city, and with the right to use the track laid down on said
Hoff street, between said Chestnut and Daley streets, and lay a third rail along
the same, upon payment of one-half of the cost of construction thereof.

Provided, and on condition that no poles are to be used in conducting the
electricity on said road, and that two horses or mules, if any, Shall be used to
each car: and that the said grantee, or his successors or assigns shall plank,
pave or macadamize the whole of said road between the rails, and for two feet
on each side thereof, and provide it for its entire length with wooden stringers
not less than four inches wide spiked to the ties against the outside of and up
to and flush with the top of the rail, and shall keep the same constantly in
repair, flush with the grade of the street and provided with good crossings for
all kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary and proper flumes for the free
passage of water under said track, and that there be sufficient space between
the tracks and sidetracks or turnouts, to allow the cars of said road to pass each
other freely and without danger; and that the width of said track shall not be
greater than four feet eight and one-half inches between the rails.

Provided, further, that the roadbed and track shall conform in all cases
where a grade has been established, to such grade, and in all other cases, to
the natural grade of the streets through which they run, and when at any time
the whole or any part of said route shall be either graded, paved or otherwise
improved, or the grade or improvement thereof changed or altered, the bed of
the road and the tracks thereof shall be, by the grantee or assignee, if so
required by said City Council or its successors, made to conform, in grade or
material, or both, therewith.

And provided, further, that no turnouts or switches shall be constructed in
places other than those designated by said City Council, or its successors, which
authority also shall prescribe the radii of curves to be used in swinging the line
of said road from one street to another.

And provided, further, that at no time shall the fare for any distance along
said road exceed the sum of five cents for one passenger; and that persons who
attend the public schools, as pupils, shall be required to pay but’
one-half of said fare on any of its cars, from or to said schools; provided, said
pupils shall purchase their fare in quantities of at least one dollar’s worth at a
time; and said grantee or his assigns shall provide for and sell such fares to said
pupils, or for their benefit, at all times when solicited so to do.

And provided, further, that the grantee or assigns of said road shall, on
or before the fifteenth day of December of each year, pay to said city such
license fee upon each car as may be required by the ordinances of said city.

===== PDF PAGE 292 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 285

And provided, further, that if at any time, for the space of six months,
the said road, or any portion thereof, shall be unused as a street railroad, the
franchise for the portions so unused shall be thereby forfeited.

Sec. 2. It is understood and agreed, that the city expressly reserves the
right to use and control all its public streets for any and all purposes, the same
as if no such franchise existed ; such use to be made so as to obstruct or injure said
road as little as possible; and when work upon, or other use of said streets
makes the same necessary, the grantee or assigns of said road shall shift the
same at their own expense, so as to avoid the obstruction made thereby. It is
further understood that throughout the entire route granted said road, the center
of the street, or a line as near thereto as practicable, is intended ; and it is
further understood that the grant of this right carries with it the right to con-
struct, lay down, maintain and operate a single track along the route of and for
the uses of said road. /

Sec. 3. The above rights and privileges are granted upon the express con-
dition that the said road shall be commenced and completely equipped and in
full running order and operation within twelve months from the date of the tak-
ing effect of this ordinance, and any failure to complete said road within the
time above prescribed, shall operate as a forfeiture of the right of way over any
portion of the same then uncompleted.

Furthermore, this franchise is expressly granted upon each and all of the
provisions and conditions herein contained, and if said grantee or his assigns
shall fail in any particular to comply therewith, then and in that case all rights
under this ordinance shall thereupon and immediately be forfeited, and this
grant shall thereupon be null and void, and nothing herein contained shall be
construed as granting an exclusive franchise.

Src. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
TripunE, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of April 25, 1887.

FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 6th day of May, 1887.
W. H. WORKMAN,

Mayor. .

the track shall not exceed seven-eighths of an inch over the entire route, viz. :

Commencing at the intersection of Mission road with Macy street; thence
along Mission road to its intersection with Griffin avenue; thence along Griffin
avenue to its intersection with Patrick street.

Provided and on condition, that the said grantees, or their successors or

rails, and for two feet on each side thereof, and provide it for its entire length
with wooden stringers, not less than four inches wide, spiked to the ties, against
the outside of and up to and flush with the top of the rail, and shall keep the
same constantly in repair, flush with the grade of the street, and provided with
good crossings for all kinds of vehicles, and with all necessary and proper flumes
for the free passage of water under said track, and that there be sufficient space
‘between the tracks and side tracks, or turnouts, to allows the cars of said
road to pass each other freely and without danger; and that the width of said
track shall not be greater than four feet eight and one-half inches between the
rails.

the natural grade of the streets through which they run; and when at any time
the whole or any part of said route shall be either graded, paved or otherwise
improved, or the grade or improvements thereof changed or altered, the bed of

And provided, further, that no turnouts or switches shall be constructed in

the street impassable for traffic, the grantees or assignees shall make a suitable
and safe carriage way though the streets over such portion.

ORDINANCE No. 312.

An Orprnance forbidding the connecting of rain water conductors gith sewers.

’

The Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, do ordain as follows:

Section 1. It shall be uulawful for any person, firm or corporation to
connect any roof-conductor, yard drain or other vehicle used for carrying off
rain or surface water, with any public sewer of the City of Los Angeles, or
house drain leading thereto.

Sec. 2. Any person, firm or corporation having the control, either as
owner or lessee of premises where roof-conductors or other vehicles for carrying
rain or surface water are connected with public sewers or house drains running
thereto, shall disconnect the same within thirty days after the passage of this

ordinance. ;

Src. 3. Any person or persons who shall refuse to comply with or shall
violate any provisions of this ordinance, shall be deemed guilty of a misde-

meanor, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be fined not to exceed one hundred
dollars, or imprisoned not more than thirty days.

===== PDF PAGE 296 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 289

Src. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this ordi-
nance, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
TripuneE, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing ordinance was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of May 16, 1887.

RESOLUTION No. 222.

A Reso.ution of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, fixing the -
salaries of the Captain of Police and the policemen of said city.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That from and after the first day of January, A. D. 1884, there
shall be allowed and paid as salaries and compensation, to the several officers
named, the following sums:

To the Captain of Police, the sum-of one hundred dollars per month.
To the policemen, not to exceed twenty-one in number, as follows:

To each horse or mounted policeman, and not to exceed six in number,
the sum of ninety-five dollars per month,

To each foot policeman, the sum of eighty dollars per month.

Sec. 2. All resolutions or parts of resolutions in conflict with this reso-
lution are hereby repealed.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
fution, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Hrraxp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of Decemher 31, 1883.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.
Approved this 12th day of January, 1884.
$ C. E. THOM,
Mayor.
Published Jaunary 17, 1884.

Hera.p, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

RESOLUTION No. 225.
A Reso.uTion accepting certain work and improvement on Hill street.
Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That the work and improvement done and made in furnishing,
laying and constructing that sewer on Hill street, known as section two of the
Hill and Seventh streets sewer, are hereby accepted.

Src. 2. That the contractor for said work, W. J. Neely, has done and
made the said work and improvement in accordance with law and the orders of
the Council, and his contract therefor.

Src. 3. That the Superintendent of Streets is hereby directed to isssue to
said contractor, W. J. Neely, a certificate that said work and improvement have
been completed according to the contract of said W. J. Neely therefor, and
accepted by this Council.

Src. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

6, 1883.

RESOLUTION No. 230.*

Reso.ution of intention to improve and grade Washington street from Figueroa |
street to the west boundary of the City of Los Angeles.

===== PDF PAGE 320 =====
 

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 303

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That it iy the intention of the Mayor and Council of the City
of Los Angeles to cause to be improved and graded, at the expense of the
property owners, Washington street from Figueroa street to the west boundary
of the city of Los Angeles in the following manner:

The road bed shall be graded and covered with eight inches of gravel
raked free of coarse stones of more than two inches in diameter, and it shall be
made to conform to the established grade at the center of the street with the
proper slope towards the curb; after being graveled it shall be thoroughly wet
and then rolled.

The curb shall be of redwood 3x12 inches, placed with the upper edge to
the established grade and spiked to posts of redwood 4x4 inches, three feet
long, set into the ground full length below the top of the curb and inside of the
same and not more than four feet apart and one to each joint of the curbing.

The sidewalks shall be 16 feet wide, graded and covered with three inches
of firm gravel, smoothly laid and raked free of coarse stones of more than one
inch in diameter. The slope of the sidewalks shall be three inches towards the
curb.

Sec. 2. That the exterior boundaries of the district of land to be affected
or benefitted by said work or improvement, and to be assessed to pay the costs
and expenses thereof, are as follows: :

Commencing at the point of intersection of the west boundary of Figueroa
street with the center line of Washington street, and running thence along the
west boundary of Figueroa street northerly 100 feet; thence on a line parallel
to the center liné of Washington street westerly 4,327 feet; thence along the
west boundary of the city southerly 227 feet; thence alonga line parallel to the
center line of Washington street easterly 4,300 feet to the west boundary of
Figueroa street ; thence northerly 100 feet to the point of beginning.

Sec. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of February 4, 1884.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

RESOLUTION No. 233.*

Reso.ution of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, providing |
regulations for hacks, job wagons, trucks, drays, etc., and for public stands
for the same.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles as follows:

Srction 1. Every vehicle, except railroad cars, which shall be used for
the conveyance of persons by land from place to place for hire shall be deemed
a hackney carriage within the meaning of this resolution.

Src. 2. Every vehicle which shall be used for the conveyance of goods,
packages or freight from place to place in this city for hire, (except hand carts,
and except also the vehicles used by merchants, dealers and manufacturers
exclusively for the delivery of their wares to customers,) shall be deemed a job
wagon within the meaning of this resolution. ‘

Sec. 8. Every vehicle which shall be used for the conveyance of wood,

~vyegetables, farm products or other merchandise intended for sale, shall be
deemed a market wagon within the meaning of this resolution.

Sec. 4. Lot eight, block thirty-eight, Ord’s:survey, in the city of Los ©
Angeles, is hereby designated as a public stand for the use of market wagons
used for the conveyance of hay. Los Angeles street, between First and Re- .
quena streets, is hereby designated as a ;ublic stand for the use of market
wagons used for the conveyance of wood.

For the use of all other market wagons not included in the two foregoing
clauses and for the use of all hackney carriages and job wagons, the streets

===== PDF PAGE 324 =====
OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 307

surrounding the public plaza east of Main street and north of the Pico House
are hereby designated as a public stand; provided, that said last aforesaid
public stand shall extend from the outer edge of the fence surrounding said
plaza only thirty feet outward.

Sec. 5. In addition to the foregoing public stands the following places are
hereby designated as lawful stands for hackney carriages and job wagons in
this city, to-wit :

Any part of any street, except as herein provided, in the City of Los
Angeles where the owner or owners of property fronting on the said part of said
street shall permit the said hackney carriage, carriages or job wagons to stand ;
but in no case shall any hackney carriage, carriages or job wagons be allowed
to block up any part of any street, or interfere with the business or travel or
commerce of the public.

Sec. 6. No person having charge of any hackney carriage, job wagon or
market wagon shall allow the same to stand within ten feet of any crossing,
nor at any greater distance than two feet from the outer edge of any sidewalk.

Sec. 7. No person having the charge or control of any hackney carriage,
job wagon or market wagon shall occupy as a stand for the same any portion
of any street in front of any building or vacant lot where the width of said
street is fifty feet or less, or when the owners of such building or vacant lot or
the occupant of the street floor of such building shall object.

And provided, further, that nothing in this resolution shall prevent any
owner or driver of any hackney carriage from stopping at any place other than
a crossing for the purpose of taking up or putting down a passenger or passen-
gers with their baggage, in whose service such hackney carriage was at the
time actually employed; and provided, further, that nothing in this resolution
shall prevent the owner or driver of a job wagon or market wagon from stopping
any place, other than a public crossing, of any public street from one sidewalk

to another for the purpose of receiving or delivering any goods, wares or mer-
chandise.

And provided, further, that hackney carriages and job wagons may stand

in front of real property owned or rented by the owner of said hackney carriages
or wagons on streets more than fifty feet wide.

Src. 8. Whenever several hackney carriages shall attend at any place for
or with passengers the Chief of Police, or any regular or special policeman,
may give directions respecting the standing of such carriages while waiting for,

taking or putting down passengers, and every driver of such carriage shall
conform ‘to and comply with such directions.

===== PDF PAGE 325 =====
3808 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 9. All persons are hereby prohibited from using any part of the
streets of the city of Los Angeles as a stopping place for any hackney carriages,
job wagons, trucks, drays or other vehicles, except as hereinbefore provided.

Sec. 10. Any person violating, refusing or neglecting to comply with the
provisions of this resolution shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on
conviction, be fined not less than five dollars, nor more than thirty dollars, or
be imprisoned in the County Jail not less than two days, nor more than ten
days, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Src. 11. All ordinances, resolutions and parts of ordinances and resolu-
tions in conflict with this resolution are hereby repealed.

Src. 12. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of February 11, 1884.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 15th day of February, 1884.

free of coarse stones of more than two inches in diameter, and it shall be made

slope towards the curb, and after being graveled it shall be thoroughly wet and

the established grade, and spiked to posts of redwood, 4x4 inches, three feet

granite cobblestones, not less than twelve inches long and not more than six
inches in diameter, thoroughly set in sand and then rammed. The center of
the gutter shall be twelve inches and the outer edge be six inches below the
grade.

The sidewalks shall be ten feet wide, graded and covered with three inches
of fine gravel smoothly laid and raked free from coarse stones of more than one
inch in diameter. The slope of the sidewalks shall be three inches towards
the curb.

line of Flower street ; thence along the east boundary of Flower street southerly

RESOLUTION No. 244.

Resouution of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, providing

regulations for hacks, job wagons, trucks, drays, etc., and for public stands
*for the same.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles as follows:

Section 1. Every vehicle, except railroad cars, which shall be used for
. the conveyance of persons by land from place to place for hire shall be deemed
a hackney carriage within the meaning of this resolution.

Sec. 2. Every vehicle which shall be used for the conveyance of goodb,
packages or freight from place to place in this city for hire, (except hand carts,
and except also the vehicles used by merchants, dealers and manufacturers
exclusively for the delivery of their wares to customers), shall be deemed a job
wagon within the meaning of this resolution.

Sec. 3. Every vehicle which shall be used in the conveyance of wood,
vegetables, farm products or other merchandise intended for sale, shall be
deemed a market wagon within the meaning of this resolution.

Src. 4. Los Angeles street, between Arcadia street and Fifth street, is
hereby designated as a public stand for the use of market wagons used for
the conveyance of hay.

Los Angeles street, between First and Arcadia streets, is hereby designated

as a jlblic stand for the use of market wagons used for the conveyance of
wood.

4

For the use of all other market wagons not included in the two foregoing
clauses and for the use of all hackney carriages and job wagons, the streets
surrounding the public plaza east of Main street and north of the be House
are hereby designated as a public stand; provided, that said last aforesaid
public stand shall extend from the outer edge of the fence surrounding said
plaza only thirty feet outward.

Src. 5. In addition to the foregoing public stands the following places are
hereby designated as lawful stands for hackney carriages and job wagons in
this city, to-wit:

===== PDF PAGE 338 =====
be

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. Sz tk

Any part of any street, except as herein provided, in the City of Los
Angeles where the owner or owners of property fronting on the said part of said
street shall permit the said hackney carriage, carriages or job wagons to stand ;
but in no case shall any hackney carriage, carriages or job wagons be allowed
to block up any part of any street, or interfere with the business or travel or
commerce of the public.

Src. 6. No person having charge of any hackney carriage, job wagon or
market wagon shall allow the same to stand within ten feet of any crossing,
nor at any greater distance than two feet from the outer edge of any sidewalk.

Sec. 7. No person haying the charge or control of any hackney carriage,
job wagon or market wagon shall occupy as.a stand for the same any portion
of any street in front of any building or vacant lot where the width of such
street is fifty feet or less, or when the owners of such building or vacant lot or
the occupant of the street floor of such building shall object.

And provided, further, that nothing in this resolution “shall prevent any
owner or driver of any hackney carriage from stopping at any place other than
a crossing for the purpose of taking up or putting down a passenger or passen-
gers with their baggage, in whose service such hackney carriage was at the
time actually employed; and provided, further, that nothing in this resolution
shall prevent the owner or driver of a job wagon or market wagon from stopping
at any place, other than a public crossing, of any public street from one sidewalk

to another for the purpose of receiving or delivering any goods, wares or mer-
chandise.

And provided, further, that hackney carriages and job wagons may stand

in front of real property owned or rented by the owner of said hackney carriages
or wagons on streets more than fifty feet wide. :

Sec. 8. Whenever several hackney carriages shall attend at any place for
or with passengers the Chief of Police, or any regular or special policeman,
may give directions respecting the standing of such carriages while waiting for,
taking or putting down passengers, and every driver of such carriage shall
conform to and comply with such directions.

Sec. 9. All persons are hereby prohibited from using any part of the
streets of the City of Los Angeles as a stopping place for any hackney carriages,
job wagons, trucks, drays or other vehicles, except as hereinbefore provided.

Sec. 10. Any person violating, refusing or neglecting to comply with the
provisions of this resolution shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on
conviction, be fined not less than five dollars nor more than thirty dollars, or

be imprisoned in the city jail not less than two days nor more than ten days,
or by both such fine and imprisonment.

===== PDF PAGE 339 =====
322 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Src. 11. All ordinances, resolutions » 4 parts of ordinances and resolu-
tions in conflict with this resolution are hereby repealed.

Sec. 12. ,The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heratp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of March 17, 1884.

W. W. ROBINSON,

RESOLUTION No. 267.

A Resoxution forbidding the manufacture or preparation of tripe, glue or other
noxious, injurious or offensive articles.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. All persons are hereby prohibited from preparing or manu-
facturing tripe, glue or other noxious, injurious or offensive article or substance
in the limits of the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 2. Anyone violating the provisions of this resolution shall, upon
conviction, be punished by a fine of not less than ten nor more than two hun-
dred dollars, or by imprisonment in the City Jail not less than ten days nor
more than six months, or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Src. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and shall couse the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon and thereafter shall take effect and be in force.

RESOLUTION No. 284.

A Resoxution forbidding persons not policemen from wearing a policeman’s
badge, and from wearing anything resembling a policeman’s badge.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. All persons not policemen of this city, or not duly authorized
by law, are hereby prohibited from wearing in the City of Los Angeles any star
or badge, or other thing, of the pattern, design or in the resemblance of that
star or badge adopted, or that may hereafter be adopted, by the Board of Police
Commissieners of the City of Los Angeles for the use of the Police Department
of the City of Los Angeles, and are hereby prohibited from wearing any star or
badge or other thing likely to be confounded with that gtar or badge adopted, or
to be hereafter adopted, by said Board of Police Commissioners for said Police
Department.

Sec. 2. Any person violating any provisions of this resolution shall be
guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall, on conviction, be punished by a fine of not
less than ten dollars and not more than five hundred dollars, or by imprison-
ment in the City Jail for not less than ten days and not more than six months,
or by both such fine and imprisonment.

Sec. 3. All resolutions and parts of resolutions in conflict with this resolu-
tion are hereby repealed.

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heratp; and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of May 26, 1884.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 28th day of May, 1884.

C. E. THOM,
Mayor.
Published June 6, 1884.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That there be and hereby is ordered to be graded and improved,

section three of this resolution, Seventh street from Pearl street to Alvarado
street, in the following manner:

The roadbed shall be graded and covered with eight inches of gravel, raked
free of coarse stones of more than two inches in diamter, and it shall be made
to conform to the established grade at the center of the street, with the proper
slope towards the curb; after being graveled, it shall be thoroughly wet and
then rolled.

The curb shall be of redwood, 3x12 inches, placed with the upper edge to
the established grade, and spiked to posts of redwood, 4x4 inches, three feet
long, set into the ground full length below the top of the curb and inside of the
same, and not more than four feet apart, and one to each joint of the curbing,

The gutter shall be three and one-half feet wide, concave at the bottom,
and paved with granite cobble stones not less than twelve inches long and not
more than six inches in diameter, thoroughly set in sand and then rammed;
the center of the gutter shall be twelve inches, and the outer edge shall be six
inches below the grade.

The sidewalks shall be twelve feet wide, graded and covered with three inches
of fine gravel smoothly laid and raked free from coarse stones of more than one
inch in diameter. The slope of the sidewalks shall be three inches towards
the curb.

There shall be three wooden culverts, 5 feet by four feet, inner dimensions,
constructed across said Seventh street, in accordance with the plans in the
office of the City Surveyor, viz: One at a point 589 feet west from Pearl street,
and one at a point 1,530 feet west from Pearl street, and one at a point. 2,430
feet west from Pearl street; but the bids at so much per lineal foot shall not
include said culverts, it having been ordered by the Honorable Council that
said culverts shall be built and constructed at the expense of the city.

Src. 2. The said work and improvement shall be divided into three
sections, as follows:

SECTION ONE.

From west boundary of Pearl street to a point on Seventh street, 1,900 feet
west of the west boundary of Pearl street.

RESOLUTION No. 297.

Resouvtion prohibiting the destruction or injury of public parks, or other city
property, within the limits of the City of Los Angeles.

Be it resolyed by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. It shall be unlawful, and all persons are hereby prohibited
from defacing, breaking, destroying or removing any works of art, or any public
works erected on any of the public parks, or other city property, by the City of
Los Angeles, without first obtaining permission of the Council so to do.

Sec. 2. All persons are hereby prohibited from lying down upon the grass
plots of any public parks or public grounds belonging to the City of Los Angeles.

Sec. 8. Every person is hereby prohibited from defacing, breaking, de-
stroying or removing any ornamental plant, tree, shrub, bush or flower grow-
ing upon, or any personal property of any kind, in any public park or public
grounds of said City of Los Angeles. ;

Sec. 4. Any person violating any of the provisions of this resolution shall
be punished, on conviction thereof, by a fine of not exceeding one hundred
dollars.

lution and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily

one-hundredths (1139.60) dollars.

subject to the following provisions, to-wit:

That any person or persons who have performed labor upon, or furnished
materials for the construction of said work or improvement, may file, within
said fifteen days, with the said City Treasurer of the City of Los Angeles, any
written claim or claims he or they may make on account of such labor per-
formed or materials furnished; and at the expiration of said fifteen days
said City Treasurer shall pay to said contractor the amount specified in this
resolution, less the aggregate amount of all such claims, if any, filed in accord-
ance with the provisions of Section 15 of “‘An Act to provide for the improve-
ment of streets, lanes, alleys, courts, places and sidewalks, and the construction
of sewers within municipalities,’’ approved March 6, 1883.

Should any money be retained by said City Treasurer on account of any such
claim or claims he shall pay over the amount of each claim only upon the
the order therefor of said contractor endorsed by the claimant thereof, or
upon the order therefor of any court of competent jurisdiction.

Srction 1. Whereas, the People of the State of California, represented in
Senate and Assembly, did, by act approved February 28, 1876, enact a law
entitled “‘An Act to authorize the corporation, the Mayor and Common Council
of the City of Los Angeles, to issue bonds and to provide means for the improve-

Whereas, in pursuance of the provisions of said act, the Common Council of

i

the City of Los Angeles did cause to be issued bonds of the City of Los Angeles
payable the Ist day of April, 1896, and bearing interest at the rate of seven per

ance with the provisions of said act; and,

Whereas, there is now in the Interest and Sinking Fund provided for by
section 3 of said act the sum of eleven thousand one hundred and thirty-eight
11-100 dollars to be applied to the redemption of said bonds ; ‘

e

Therefore be it resolved, That the City Treasurer of the City of Los Angeles

RESOLUTION No. 337.

A Resoxution declaring the intention of the City of Los Angeles to purchase
the remaining interest of Griffith Jenkins Griffith in the waters of the Los
Angeles River, and directing notice thereof to be given.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles as follows:

Section 1. Whereas, The City of Los Angeles upon the 30th day of August,

===== PDF PAGE 442 =====
 

4924 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

1884, entered into an agreement with Griffith Jenkins Griffith whereby the
City of Los Angeles was given the privilege of purchasing the remaining interest
of said Griffith Jenkins Griffith in those certain water rights belonging or
claimed to belong to him as appurtenant to the Los Feliz Rancho, and the said
Griffith made a deed in trust of his remaining interest in the waters of the Los
Angeles River to E. F. Spence and I. W. Hellman, with power to convey the
same to the City of Los Angeles upon certain conditions; and,

Whereas, The conditions of said agreement and of said Deed of Trust were
that the said City of Los Angeles should give notice to the said Griffith on or
before the Ist day of April, 1885, of its intention to purchase this said remaining
interest in said water right, and should on or before the 15th day of September,
1885, pay to the said Griffith therefor the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars
in gold coin, or by warrant upon the Treasurer of the City of Los Angeles; and

Whereas it is for the best interests of the City of Los Angeles that such
purchase be made; therefore be it

Resolved, That the City of Los Angeles purchase the said remaining interest
of the said Griffith Jenkins Griffith in the water rights belonging or claimed to
belong to him as appurtenant to the Los Feliz Rancho as described in the said
agreement and Trust Deed, and in accordance with the terms of said agreement.

Src. 2. The Clerk of the Council be and is hereby directed to prepare a
written notice that the City of Los Angeles intends to purchase the said
remaining interest of said Griffith Jenkins Griffith in said water rights in —
accordance with the terms of said agreement, and cause said notice to be served
upon the said Griffith Jenkins Griffith personally within ten days after the
taking effect of this resolution, or if the said Griffith cannot be found the Clerk
shall cause the said notice to be left at said Griffith’s residence between the
hours of eight in the morning and six in the evening, with some person of
suitable age and discretion, and shall also put a copy of said notice enclosed in

an envelope, postage prepaid, into the Postoffice directed to said Griffith
Jenkins Griffith.

Src. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heraxp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council
of the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of March 10, 1885.

RESOLUTION No. 353.

A Resouution of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles regulating
the rate at which water for irrigation shall be sold on and after August 1,
1885.

Be it resolyed by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles as follows: 7
Section 1. On and after August 1st, the rates for water sold for irrigation

within the city limits shall be as follows, viz. :
For one head, per day, $3.

For one head, per night, $2.

Sec. 2. The charge for use or water outside of city limits, shall be as
follows :

For one head, per day, $5.
e
For one head, per night, $3.

' Sec. 8. The rates for fractions of days shall be proportioned to the rate
for whole days, as applied to sections Nos. 1 and 2, provided that in no case
water shall be sold for less time than half a day or half a night.

Sec. 4, The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.
