RESOLUTION No. 355.

A Reso.ution providing for the holding of a special election, at which shall be
submitted to a vote of the people the question of issuing bonds of the City
of Los Angeles, to raise money for the purpose of making certain necessary
public improvements.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. Whereas, it is deemed expedient to issue bonds of the City of
Los Angeles to the amount of two hundred and forty-five thousand dollars, _
bearing interest at six per cent. and redeemable on or before twenty years —
from the date of the issue thereof, to raise money for the purpose of making a
certain necessary public improvements, as specified in Ordinance No. 175 of the
City of Los Angeles, entitled ‘‘An Ordinance to provide forthe issue of bonds
for the purpose of making certain necessary improvements,” approved July 6
1885; and 4

Whereas said bonds cannot be issued without the assent of two-thirds of —
the qualified electors of the City of Los Angeles voting at an election held for
that purpose, now therefore be it

Resolved, that a special election be held in the City of Los Angeles on
Monday, the 17th day of August, 1885, at which shall be submitted to the
qualified electors of said city the question of issuing six per cent. bonds of the
City of Los Angeles to the amount of two hundred and forty-five thousand —
dollars, redeemable on or before twenty years from the date of the issue thereof,

for the purpose of raising money for the making of the i SPT yonneaes specified
in the ordinance hereinbefore referred in this section.

Src. 2. The following places for said election shall be as follows:

RESOLUTION No. 364.

A Reso.vtion requesting an early hearing by the Supreme Court of the appli-
cation in ex-parte Guerrero.

Section 1. Whereas we have just learned that the Supreme Court has
fixed the hearing of ex-parte Guerrero for next January, and

Whereas, an immediate determination of that case is of vitalimportanceto _

Los Angeles City, as well as to all concerned, and any delay in finally deter- — .

mining the power of the City in the premises will be against public interest,
and a serious embarrassment to said municipality; and further remembering —
that this city has never before requested of the Supreme Court a similar favor;
therefore be it f

Resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, that the
Honorable the Supreme Court of this State is respectfully and earnestly
requested to set the hearing of said matter for as early a day as practicable, if
possible not later than Monday next; and the City Attorney is instructed to
forward this preamble and resolution, properly certified, to the Clerk of said —
Court, that the same may be duly presented.

Sec. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heratp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council
of the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of December 1, 1885. ‘

RESOLUTION No. 371.

A REsoLution requesting of the Supreme Court an early determination of the
case of ex-parte Guerrero.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles as follows:

Whereas the case of ex-parte Guerrero, now pending the Supreme Court
of the State of California, involves the validity of Ordinance No. 194 of tle City
of Los Angeles, providing for the licensing of business carried on in said
city ; and

Whereas the uncertainty as to the validity of said ordinance interferes
with the collection of a great portion of the revenue of said city ; and

Whereas it is of great importance to the city and to all the business interests
thereof that the question in dispute concerning the validity of said ordinance

be determined at an early date. Therefore be it resolved,

Section 1. That the Supreme Court be requested to give the case of ex-

. parte Guerrero as early consideration and decision as the business of the Court

will permit.

Suc. 38. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to a copy of the resolution

===== PDF PAGE 476 =====
458 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

and transmit the same to the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the State
of California.

Sec. 2. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Heracp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council
of the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of January 12, 1886.

W. W. ROBINSON,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

RESOLUTION No. 372.
Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Whereas, at a regular meeting of the Council of the City of Los Angeles,
held January 19th, 1886, a committee from the Los Angeles Board of Trade
appeared before the Council; and 4

support a petition to Congress on the part of Los Angeles Board of Trade
asking for the appropriation of the following amounts to-wit: $250,000 for the
completion of the work of improvement of Wilmington Harbor, as estimated
by Col. Geo. H. Mendall, U. 8. A.in charge of the work; $250,000 for the con-
struction of a Government building in this city; and for the passage of an act
authorizing the establishment of a United States District Court in this city
for the District comprised in Los Angeles, San Diego, San Bernardino, Santa
Barbara, San Luis Obispo, Ventura and Kern Counties. Therefore be it
resolved,

Section 1. That the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles, as the
representatives of 32,000 citizens, unanimously concur in and heartily endorse

the statement of facts as to the vital importance of these questions to ourentire —

city, and respectfully and strongly urge upon Congress that at its present
session it will take the necessary steps to fulfil the request of the Los Angeles
Board of Trade.

RESOLUTION No. 384.

A Reso.ution authorizing the advertising for and redemption of certain bonds
of the City of Los Angeles.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles as follows:

SEcTION 1. Whereas, the people of the State of California, represented in
Senate and Assembly, did, by an Act approved February 28, A. D. 1876, enact
a law entitled ‘‘An Act to authorize the corporation, the Mayor and Common
Council of the City of Los Angeles to issue bonds and to provide means for the
improvement of irrigation in said city, which Act was to take effect immedi-
diately,’’ and whereas, in pursuance of the provisions of said Act, the Common
Council of the City of Los Angeles did cause to be issued bonds of the City of
Los Angeles, payable the first day of April, A. D. 1896, and bearing interest
at the rate of seven per cent. per annum, which bonds were all duly signed,
issued and sold in accordance with the provision of said Act.

And whereas, there is now in the Interest and Sinking Fund, provided for
by section three of said Act, the sum of eleven thousand six hundred and
thirty-one and eleven one-hundredth dollars, to be applied to the redemption of
said bonds; therefore, be it

Resolved, that the City Treasurer of the City of Los Angeles be and is
hereby directed to advertise for four weeks in the Los Angeles Daily Heraup
for sealed proposals, to be opened at the session of the Council of said city next
ensuing after the last publication thereof, for the surrender of bonds issued
under said Act, which advertisement shall state the amount of money hd has
on hand for the purpose of redemption, and reserve to the Council the right to
reject any or all bids.

Sec. 2. When proposals are opened, the Council shall accept the lowest
proposals at rates not exceeding par value, or may redeem the greatest amount
of bonds until the cash on hand for redemption is exhausted, or reject all bids.

Sec. 3. The surrender of said bonds, in pursuance of the provisions of this
resolution, shall exonerate the City Treasurer from all liability to the City of

===== PDF PAGE 492 =====
AT4 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

_Los Angeles, by reason of the payment made by him for the bonds so sur-
rendered.

/

Sec. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-_
lution, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Herarp, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles at its meeting of March 9, 1886.

Approved this 15th day of March, 1886.

RESOLUTION No. 439.
A Resotction regulating the granting of franchises.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. Hereafter, no franchise shall be granted to any person or cor
poration for any purpose until such person or corporation shall have executed
and delivered to the City of Los Angeles a bond, with two or more sureties, to
be approved by the Mayor and Council, in the penal sum of ten thousand —
(10,000) dollars, conditioned that such person, corporation, or its assigns shall
comply with all the conditions of the ordinance granting such franchise.

lution, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Hegavp and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

RESOLUTION No. 497.

Resouution ordering the laying out and construction of a branch public sewer
on Main street extension, to be known as the Main Street Extension Sewer
No. 1.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That there be and hereby is ordered to be laid out and con-
structed a branch public sewer, to be a public sewer of the City of Los Angeles,
and to be known and designated as the Main Street Extension Sewer No. 1,
along and over the following described route :

Commencing at Marchessault street, and running northerly along Main
street extension to the Alameda street sewer, as per map and profile on file in
the City Surveyor’s office.

The said sewer shall be constructed of vitrified iron stone or of glazed pipe,
of the clear inside diameter of eight inches, and to be constructed in
accordance with the plans and specifications in office of the City Surveyor of
Los Angeles.

The cost of the construction of said sewer shall be paid out of the General
Sewer Fund of the City of Los Angeles.

RESOLUTION No, 502.

A ResouuTion authorizing the advertising for and redemption of certain Bonds
of the City of Los Angeles.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. Whereas, the people of the State of California, represented in
Senate and Assembly, did, by an act approved February 28, A. D. 1876, enact
a law entitled an act to authorize the Corporation, the Mayor and Common
Council of the City of Los Angeles to issue bonds and to provide means for
the improvement of irrigation in said city, which act was to take effect im-
mediately ; and :

Whereas, in pursuance of the provisions of said act, the Common Council
of the City of Los Angeles did cause to be issued bonds of the City of Los
Angeles, payable on the Ist day of April, A. D. 1896, and bearing interest at
the rate of seven per cent. per annum, which bonds were all duly signed,
issued and sold in accordance with the provisions of said act; and

===== PDF PAGE 612 =====
*

OF THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES. 593

Whereas, there is now in the Interest and Sinking Fund, provided for by
section 3 of said Act, the sum of eleven thousand two hundred and eighty-eight
forty-hundredths dollars, to be applied to the redemption of said bonds; there-
fore be it

Resolved, That the City Treasurer of the City of Los Angeles, be and he is
hereby directed to advertise for four weeks in the Los Angeles Trreune for
sealed proposals, to be opened at the session of the Council of said City next
ensuing after the last publication thereof, for the surrender of bonds issued
under said act, which advertisement shall state the amount of money he has
on hand for the purpose of redemption, and reserve to the Council the right to
reject any or all bids.

Sec. 2. When proposals are opened, the Council shall accept the lowest
proposals, at rates not exceeding par value, as may redeem the greatest amount
of bonds, until the cash on hand for redemption is exhausted, or reject all bids.

Sec. 3. The surrender of said bonds, in pursuance of the provisions of
this resolution, shall exonerate the City Treasurer from all liability to the City
of Los Angeles, by reason of the payment made by him for the bonds so sur-
rendered.

Src. 4. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
Tripune, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of February 28, 1887.

FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 2d day of March, 1887.

W. H. WORKMAN,
Mayor.

Published March 3, 1887.

RESOLUTION No. 511.

ResoivtTion of the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles designating
the portion of Spring street to be improved and paved.

Be it resolved by the Meyor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1. That Spring street, in the City of Los Angeles, between its
intersection with Main street, near Temple street and its intersection with
Main street near Ninth street, and including said intersections, be and
the same is hereby ordered to be prepared and paved with asphaltum or
granite block pavements, according to the plans and specifications filed with
the Clerk of the Council, or with such other materials and in such manner
as may be determined by the owners of property abutting on said street
and other persons and parties in interest liable for the cost of said im-
provement, at a meeting held for that purpose, said meeting of said property
owners and others in interest to be held on a day to be fixed by the Council of
said city and in the manner by said Council designated. Should said propeity
owners and others in interest, at said meeting, fail to agree as to the material
to be used in the paving of said street, or the mode of paving and constructing
the same, then, and in that case, the Council shall immediately proceed to
determine all things pertaining thereto, and shall proceed therein as provided
by law.

Src. 2. The Clerk of the Council is hereby ordered to publish a notice of
this proceeding in the official newspaper of the corporation each day for the
term of ten days after the publication of this resolution.

Provided, That if within ten days after the publication of the notice of

===== PDF PAGE 621 =====
602 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

intention herein provided for, the owners of property fronting on said street,
and to be assessed for the cost of said improvements, amounting to two-thirds
of the frontage on said streets, shall make and file with the Clerk of the Council
a written remonstrance against the proposed improvement, thereupon the same
shall not be proceeded with or made.

Sec. 8. The assessments to be levied for the collection of the amount
necessary to pay the cost and expense of preparing and paving said street shall
be levied upon all the real property situated upon both sides of said Spring street,
from the intersection near Ninth street to the intersection near Temple street,
and upon the superstructures and franchises of the various street railways
maintained and running upon said street, and as in said franchises expressed.

Src. 4. If no remonstrance be filed, as herein provided, within the time
herein limited, the Clerk of the Council shall, at the expiration of said time,
advertise for sealed proposals for preparing and paving said street in accordance
with the plans and specifications determined upon and on file in his office,
together with all other work described in the specifications, and for such other
kinds of pavement, accompanied by specifications as to all details and cost as
may be presented to said Council by any person desiring to compete for the work
of preparing said street, furnishing material to be used and constructing and
completing said pavement. He shall return to the Council all bids and proposals
by him received. Should any bids for the performance of the improvement be
accepted by the Council, the same shall be immediately proceeded with as by
law provided.

Src. 3. The Clerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-

along said street amounting to two-thirds of the frontage thereon shall file with

to the plans and specifications on file in his office, and for such other work as
required by said plans and specifications, Said Clerk shall return all proposals
received by him to the Council, and in case one of said bids is accepted, then
and in that case the work shall be proceeded with as required by law.

A Resoxution designating the limits which shall include and define the im- °
mediate vicinity of improvement for which the assessment shall be paid
for the widening and improvement of Ninth street, from Main street to east
city boundary, and fixing the rate per front foot to be paid within the
limits of the immediate vicinity.

Be it resolved by the Mayor and Council of the City of Los Angeles:

Section 1, That certain street in the City of Los Angeles known as
Ninth street be widened so as to embrace and include therein as a public street
for the use of the public, all that strip or parcel of land situated in the City of
Los Angeles, County of Los Angeles, State of California, bounded and described
as follows:

Being a strip 80 feet wide lying 40 feet on each side of the following de-
scribed center line: Commencing at a granite stone monument set in the
intersection of the center line of Main street and the proposed extension of
Ninth street, and running thence along the proposed extension of Ninth street
south 42 degrees 24 minutes east, 3,423.03 feet to a cement stone set in Vejar’s
east line; thence south 48 degrees 13 minutes east, 1,316.16 feet to a cement
stone in the west line of Wolfskill street; thence south 42 degrees 31
minutes east, 2,299.41 feet to a cement stone set in the intersection of the pro-
posed extension of Ninth street and Alameda street; thence south 72 degrees
12 minutes east, 1,777.19 feet to a cement stone in the intersection of Lemon
and proposed extension of Ninth street; thence south 71 degrees 8 minutes
east, 1,605.44 feet, to a cement stone in Archibald’s east line; thence south 55
degrees 35 minutes east, 1,896.85 feet, to a cement stone in junction of the pro-
posed extension of Ninth street and Hostetter avenue; thence south 63 degrees
13 minutes east, 2,480.81 feet to a point 40 feet southerly from a 4x4 stake, the
8. E. corner of lot 6, block 70, Hancock’s survey.

Src. 2. The immediate vicinity of improvement of said street so to be
widened and improved, shall be and is hereby declared to be that portion of
said Ninth street, from the east side of Main street to the Los Angeles river.

===== PDF PAGE 651 =====
632 ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

Sec. 3. All the real property situated on the southerly side of Ninth
street within the limits hereinbefore described as the immediate vicinity of
improvement, and all the real property on the northerly side of Ninth street
within said limits, shall be and the same is hereby assessed, and the respective
owners thereof shall pay for the benefit accruing to said land by reason of said
improvements at the rate of $1.17180, and the adjacent vicinity shall pay as
provided by the charter of this city, per lineal foot frontage upon said street.

Src. 4. The widening and improvement of said street shall be made at
the expense of the property-owners fronting along said street within the limits
hereinbefore stated.

Sec. 5. TheClerk of the Council shall certify to the passage of this reso-
lution, and shall cause the same to be published once in the Los Angeles Daily
TrrpuneE, and thereupon and thereafter it shall take effect and be in force.

I hereby certify that the foregoing resolution was adopted by the Council of
the City of Los Angeles, at its meeting of June 6, 1887.

FREEMAN G. TEED,
Clerk of the Council of the City of Los Angeles.

Approved this 10th day of June, 1887.

W. H. WORKMAN,
Mayor.

Published June 11, 1887.
